job.title: Quality Assurance Officer
job.description:
Join the Team at Baiada as a Quality Assurance Officer!

Discover your full potential with Baiada, the primary poultry producer in Australia, celebrated for its iconic labels such as Steggles and Lilydale. Chandler Macleod presents an exciting opportunity for a Quality Assurance Officer to join the Beresfield Baiada team based in their Steggles production plant.

As the Quality Assurance Officer, you will be a vital part of the team, responsible for maintaining and enhancing Baiada's commitment to quality in poultry processing. This position offers consistent and full-time hours. 
 
About the Role:
As the QA Officer, your responsibilities will include but not limited to:

  • Verify cleaning and pest control activities to ensure hygiene standards are met.
  • Maintain and improve the Quality Management System.
  • Conduct internal audits and support external audit preparation and participation.
  • Verify monitoring activities during production and review completed daily paperwork.
  • Prepare product samples for laboratory testing and analyse lab results.
  • Perform data entry, filing, and reporting related to quality and hygiene.
  • Conduct end of shelf life product evaluations.
  • Carry out post clean and environmental swabbing, including Biotrace testing in RTE and fully cooked areas.
  • Perform 2-hourly cook-ups and sensory evaluations.
  • Collect product samples for quality checks.
  • Calibrate equipment including scales, Oxybaby, and thermometers.
  • Evaluate both fresh and frozen products for quality and compliance
Requirements:
  • Food Technology degree/qualification (preferred, but not essential)
  • Excellent communications skills
  • Comfortable working around raw poultry
  • Comfortable working in a refrigerated environment

Benefits:
  • Competitive hourly rate + shift allowances + daily QA allowance
  • Onsite parking for a hassle-free commute
  • Opportunities for career growth, paving the way to your success 

How to Apply:
Click APPLY or contact the Baiada Team on 02 4978 7730 for a confidential discussion, or email baiadanewcastle@chandlermacleod.com. Be part of a dynamic team where every day brings new challenges and delicious opportunities! At Chandler Macleod, we are committed to fostering a diverse workforce where everyone is welcome. We encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, women, neurodiverse, people living with a disability and the LGBTIQA+ community.

You can read more about our commitment to diversity and inclusion at https://www.chandlermacleod.com/diversity-and-inclusion.

job.title: Specialist Project Planner
job.description:
Specialist Project Planner
  • Opportunity working with Rio Tinto
  • Perth CBD 
  • 12 assignments via Chandler Macleod
  • Collaborative and safety-focused project environment
  • $109 - $121 per hour + super
About the Opportunity

Rio Tinto is a global mining and materials company focused on finding, mining and processing the natural resources that are essential to modern life. Through Chandler Macleod’s partnership with Rio Tinto, we are seeking an experienced Specialist Project Planner to join their Project Controls team.

This role is based at Central Park in Perth and will support a portfolio of major projects across the business, with site visits to the Pilbara. Working closely with project delivery, cost, estimating and contracts teams, you will play a key role in driving planning excellence, schedule integrity and project performance across a diverse project portfolio.

Reporting to the Superintendent Project Controls and working in a challenging and dynamic environment, you will:
  • Provide training and mentoring to develop resources within the team.
  • Develop and maintain company schedules in P6 to the level of detail determined by the phase maturity model.
  • Develop Basis of Schedule documents as per the company template.
  • Proactively analyse projects/programs and provide technical insight in the areas of schedule to project stakeholders.
  • Review and analyse contractors’ schedules using industry standard techniques.
  • Conduct site visits to validate progress and schedule forecast dates, discuss sequencing of the works with the site team, and identify areas of concern and potential change.
  • Ensure the Contractor and project team agree a project baseline as per contractual requirements for reporting and control purposes.
  • Review contractors progress measurement methodology and assess suitability for accurate progress measurement.
  • Assess and produce productivity reports identifying causes for deviations. 
  • Identify areas where the contractors’ schedule is non-compliant with the project controls requirements specification.
  • Review progress and performance trend information to develop internal assessment of project completion. 
  • Ensure company schedules are aligned with the company estimate and include allowances for areas of growth and contingency. 
  • Drive relationships between delivery, cost, planning, estimating and contracts groups to ensure accuracy in current trends.
  • Assist in development of key project controls improvement initiatives.
  • Drive the integrity of integrated project cost reports.
  • Support compliance with standardised processes, systems and tools.

About You
  • A commitment to the safety of yourself and your team.
  • Good understanding of schedule management techniques and methods.
  • Strong experience working within Primavera P6 scheduling software.
  • Must be a self-starter to drive and work with minimal supervision to rapidly adjust to a dynamic work environment.
  • Ability to work in a tight schedule to meet reporting cut offs.
  • Be a team player, who can work closely with project members, cutting across different levels.
  • Excellent stakeholder engagement and communication skills.
Why Join Chandler Macleod?

Chandler Macleod is one of Australia’s leading workforce solutions providers. You’ll benefit from a competitive pay rate paid weekly, superannuation on all hours worked, access to our Employee Assistance Program, a dedicated Chandler Macleod support team, streamlined onboarding processes, and opportunities for future assignments with Rio Tinto.

  • Coordinate technology teams, vendors, site representatives and corporate functions to keep delivery progressing safely, on time and within budget.

  • Provide clear and transparent reporting to Steering Committees and senior leaders on progress, risks, decisions required and readiness for future deployment.
  • Drive alignment across operational, safety, digital, technical and corporate stakeholders and produce a clear, evidence-based recommendation on next steps.

To be successful in this role, you encompass;
  • Experience delivering technology-enabled projects in operational or industrial environments.

  • Experience reporting to steering committees or executive governance forums.

  • Familiarity with enterprise technology integration will be highly regarded.
  • Experience working with SAP Analytic Cloud (SAC) will be highly regarded.

Apply now!

We are seeking a detail-oriented Quality Control Officer supporting operations in the live bay area for turkeys. This role is critical in ensuring animal welfare standards, product quality, and compliance with food safety regulations throughout all stages of production.

Passionate about producing premium quality poultry products through the Lilydale Free Range and Steggles brands, our client Baiada, have been bringing Australian families together at the dinner table since 1919!

Delivering fresh poultry to local retailers and value-adding products to Quick Service Restaurants and food service customers, Baiada are leading the way in the industry through innovation and setting high standards around process and efficiency, which ensures they deliver millions of high-quality products every year.

About the Role:
  • Monitor and assess live bird handling practices 
  • Identify and report any non-conformance issues in handling, hygiene, or processing
  • Perform routine documentation, record-keeping, and reporting of QC checks
  • Maintain high standards of cleanliness, sanitation, and workplace safety
  • Assist in audits and continuous improvement initiatives
About You: 
  • Previous experience in quality control, food production, or poultry processing preferred
  • Ability to work in a fast-paced, physically demanding environment
  • Strong attention to detail and problem-solving skills
  • Good communication and teamwork ability
  • Willingness to work around live animals and in slaughter environments
Other Requirements:
  • Ability to keep up with production demands and work effectively as part of a team
  • Physically capable of standing for long periods and carrying out repetitive tasks
  • Available to work early morning shifts - 4:00 am start
  • Holds a current driver's licence and has reliable transportation
  • Active working rights in Australia (legally entitled to work)
How to Apply:
  • Click APPLY or contact the Baiada Team on 02 4978 7730 for a confidential discussion, or email baiadanewcastle@chandlermacleod.com. Be part of a dynamic team where every day brings new challenges and delicious opportunities!

job.title: Policy and Program Managers
job.description:
Chandler Macleod is recruiting on behalf of our client for an exceptional opportunity within a high-profile Federal Government agency supporting Australia's most significant long-term capability program.

This is a unique chance for an experienced Policy and Program Manager to influence national security strategies, oversee complex policy and program initiatives, and contribute to a pivotal defence project that will shape Australia’s industrial and defence capabilities for decades to come.

About the Role
Reporting directly to the senior leadership team, the Policy and Program Manager will provide expert leadership in policy development, program management, and strategic oversight of key defence initiatives. You will be responsible for crafting high-impact policies, managing large projects, and engaging with diverse stakeholders including government agencies, industry partners, academia, and international allies to ensure the delivery of Australia’s long-term submarine and defence capabilities. This role is ideal for a detail-oriented professional with strong leadership skills and a passion for national security.

Key Responsibilities
  • Lead the development and implementation of strategic policies supporting defence industrial capabilities and workforce growth
  • Oversee complex programs, ensuring timely delivery, compliance with standards, and achievement of organisational objectives
  • Collaborate with stakeholders across government, industry, and academia to align objectives and promote industrial resilience
  • Provide high-level advice on policy impact, industrial strategies, and risk management
  • Monitor program performance, identify opportunities for improvement, and support continuous process enhancements
  • Maintain security clearances and ensure all activities meet security and confidentiality standards

About You:
You will demonstrate:
  • Extensive experience in policy development, program management, or strategic assessment within government, defence, or industrial environments
  • Strong knowledge of defence policies, industrial capabilities, workforce initiatives, and supply chain development
  • Proven ability to lead complex projects and influence stakeholders at all levels
  • Exceptional communication skills, capable of producing high-quality briefs, reports, and strategic documents
  • Demonstrated leadership qualities, strategic thinking, and sound judgment
  • Ability to obtain and maintain a Security Clearance

Applicants must be able to obtain and maintain a security clearance at “Negative Vetting Level 1”.

Apply Now
If you are a seasoned policy and program professional seeking to contribute to a critical national security program and support Australia’s future defence capabilities, we encourage you to apply today.

At Chandler Macleod, we are committed to fostering a diverse workforce where everyone is welcome. We encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, women, neurodiverse individuals, people living with a disability, and the LGBTIQA+ community. You can read more about our commitment to diversity and inclusion at https://www.chandlermacleod.com/diversity-and-inclusion.

job.title: Digital Testing Lead
job.description:
Digital Testing Lead
  • Opportunity working at Rio Tinto
  • 5-month assignment via Chandler Macleod
  • Safety-first culture with supportive teams
About the Opportunity
Rio Tinto is a global mining and materials company operating in 35 countries, producing the materials essential to modern life. Their operations are built on safety, innovation, inclusion and creating value for communities, customers and shareholders.

Through Rio Tinto’s partnership with Chandler Macleod, we are seeking an experienced Digital Testing Lead to join the Finance Digital team.

Entering the project during mid-build, the Digital Testing Lead will lead user acceptance testing for Finance Digital products and changes, making sure business users can test effectively and that the project has a clear, evidence-based view of readiness for release.

Key Responsibilities
  • Plan and coordinate UAT activities with business representatives, product owners and the delivery team.
  • Define test scenarios, test cases and acceptance criteria with the relevant business users.
  • Prepare testers, coordinate testing sessions and keep the test schedule on track.
  • Record, prioritise and follow up defects, issues and decisions arising through UAT.
  • Work with delivery and technical teams to ensure defects are understood, resolved and retested.
  • Provide clear reporting on test progress, outstanding risks and readiness for release.
  • Maintain UAT evidence, including test outcomes, defect status and business sign-off.
  • Identify gaps in test coverage or business readiness early and escalate them appropriately.

To be successful in this role, you encompass;
  • Experience leading or coordinating UAT in a business, finance, systems or digital-delivery environment.
  • Able to work comfortably with business users who have varying levels of technical confidence.
  • Strong organisation and follow-through across multiple testers, scenarios and competing priorities.
  • Clear written communication, particularly for defects, risks, test outcomes and release-readiness reporting.
  • Can demonstrate practical judgement about what needs escalation and what can be resolved within the delivery team.
  • Experience with the SAP Analytic Cloud (SAC) and SAP Business Data Cloud (BDC) will be highly regarded but not critical.

Apply now!
 If you are organised, calm under pressure and prepared to seek clarification when testing outcomes are unclear, we would love to hear from you.

job.title: Client Services Operations Manager
job.description:
Operations Manager - 24/7 Customer Service Operations 

Our client is a leading global service provider operating within a fast-paced, highly regulated, customer-facing environment. They are seeking an experienced Operations Manager to lead a large, multi-disciplinary workforce responsible for delivering exceptional customer outcomes within a complex 24/7 operation.

This is a highly visible leadership opportunity suited to an operational leader who thrives under pressure, leads from the front, and has a proven track record managing large teams, critical service delivery requirements, and key stakeholder relationships.

Whether your background is in transport, logistics, facilities management, hospitality, healthcare, retail operations or another high-volume service environment, we are keen to speak with leaders who understand how to balance people, performance and customer expectations.

The Opportunity Reporting into senior operational leadership, you will take ownership of day-to-day service delivery while ensuring operational, commercial and customer performance objectives are consistently achieved.
You will lead a team of frontline leaders and a sizeable shift-based workforce, ensuring the operation remains responsive, efficient and customer-focused, particularly during periods of peak demand, disruption and changing operational requirements.

This role requires a hands-on leader who is equally comfortable engaging with frontline employees, managing client relationships and making critical operational decisions in real time.

Key Responsibilities:
  • Lead a large operational workforce across a 24/7 environment.
  • Drive service excellence and ensure customer commitments are consistently achieved.
  • Develop and coach frontline leaders to build a high-performing, accountable culture.
  • Manage workforce planning, rostering, leave management and labour utilisation.
  • Build trusted relationships with key clients and stakeholders.
  • Monitor and improve operational KPIs, productivity and service performance.
  • Lead operational responses during incidents, service disruptions and peak demand periods.
  • Drive continuous improvement initiatives through data analysis and performance insights.
  • Manage employee relations matters including performance management, coaching and workplace investigations.
  • Champion safety, compliance and quality standards across all aspects of the operation.
  • Contribute to financial performance through effective cost control, workforce management and operational efficiency.
About You You are an experienced operations leader who has successfully managed large teams within a fast-paced service environment and understands the importance of delivering outstanding customer outcomes while maintaining operational performance.

You will bring:
  • Proven experience managing large, shift-based operational teams.
  • Strong leadership skills with the ability to motivate and develop frontline leaders.
  • Experience managing customer service delivery within a complex operational environment.
  • Demonstrated success improving operational performance and service standards.
  • Strong stakeholder management and client relationship skills.
  • Experience managing workforce planning, rostering and labour costs.
  • The ability to remain calm, decisive and solutions-focused during periods of disruption or operational pressure.
  • Sound experience dealing with employee relations, performance management and workplace compliance requirements.
  • Strong commercial acumen and a continuous improvement mindset.

job.title: School Crossing Supervisor City of Monash
job.description:
Start the New Year with a Role That Makes a Real Difference in Your Community

Are you looking for meaningful, part-time work that fits seamlessly around your lifestyle and offers excellent work–life balance? If so, our School Crossing Supervisor role could be the perfect opportunity for you.

As a School Crossing Supervisor, you will play a vital role in keeping school-aged children, families, and pedestrians safe during busy morning and afternoon school times. This is a rewarding position where you’ll become a familiar and trusted face in your local community.

Positions are available across the City of Monash, with placements offered as close to your home as possible based on operational requirements and availability.

About the role
  • Assist children and pedestrians to safely cross the road during peak school hours
  • Work outdoors and engage positively with the local community
  • Morning shifts between 8:00am – 9:00am and/or afternoon shifts between 3:00pm – 4:00pm, Monday to Friday during school terms
  • Opportunity to work at multiple locations within the council area when required
To be successful, you will
  • Be friendly, reliable, community-minded, and confident communicating with people of all ages
  • Be available for morning and/or afternoon shifts during school terms
  • Hold, or be willing to obtain, a Working With Children Check
  • Be flexible to work across different crossing locations if needed
  • Be able to pass a Police Check and Medical Clearance
What’s in it for you?
  • Part-time maximum-term contract
  • Accrual of Annual Leave and Sick/Carer’s Leave
  • Superannuation paid in addition to your hourly rate
  • Consistent hours that support work–life balance
  • A role where you genuinely contribute to community safety and wellbeing

If you’re ready to start a role that’s rewarding, flexible, and community focused, we’d love to hear from you.

job.title: Training product development and deployment specialist
job.description:
Training Product Development & Deployment Specialist
Perth CBD  
6-9 Month Contract | Immediate Start Available

An exciting opportunity exists for an experienced Training Product Development & Deployment Specialist to join a leading mining and resources company supporting a significant pipeline of training development initiatives.
This role will suit a seasoned Learning & Development professional who enjoys taking ownership of projects from concept through to deployment. You'll work closely with Subject Matter Experts (SMEs) and stakeholders to design, develop and deliver engaging learning solutions, with a strong focus on eLearning and blended learning programs supporting operational and technical workforces.

Key Responsibilities
  • Design, develop and deploy eLearning and blended learning solutions.
  • Create engaging learning content using Articulate 360, Storyline and/or Rise.
  • Work directly with SMEs to extract technical information and translate it into effective learning experiences.
  • Manage multiple learning development projects concurrently.
  • Conduct learning needs analysis and recommend appropriate learning solutions.
  • Develop facilitator guides, learner resources, assessments and supporting materials.
  • Ensure training products meet quality standards and are delivered within agreed timeframes.
  • Coordinate testing, reviews and deployment activities.
About You
  • Strong Instructional Design and Learning Design experience.
  • Hands-on experience developing eLearning content in Articulate 360, Storyline and/or Rise.
  • Proven experience delivering learning products from needs analysis through to deployment.
  • The ability to manage multiple projects and competing priorities.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement and SME consultation skills.
  • Excellent written communication and content development capabilities.
  • A proactive and autonomous approach with the ability to work with minimal supervision.
Desirable Experience
  • Experience within mining, resources, manufacturing, energy, logistics or other operational environments.
  • Experience developing facilitator-led, blended and digital learning programs.
  • Exposure to Learning Management Systems (LMS).
  • Relevant qualifications in Learning & Development, Instructional Design, Education or a related field.
What's on Offer?
  • 6-9 month contract.
  • Immediate start available.
  • Opportunity to support major training and learning initiatives within the mining sector.
  • Work closely with SMEs and key stakeholders across a large operational business.
  • Collaborative and supportive team environment.
If you're an experienced Instructional Designer, Learning Designer or eLearning Developer looking for your next contract opportunity and enjoy creating engaging learning solutions in a fast-paced environment, we'd love to hear from you.

job.title: Internal Sales & Hire Coordinator
job.description:
We are seeking a commercially minded and personable Internal Sales & Hire Coordinator to join an established plant and equipment hire business based in Dandenong South.

This is a hands-on, phone-based role focused on maintaining strong client relationships and generating dry hire opportunities across the civil and construction industries.

A large part of your day will involve proactively contacting existing and previous clients, keeping the business front of mind and understanding their upcoming projects and equipment requirements. You'll also manage inbound hire enquiries, prepare and follow up quotes, re-engage dormant clients and identify opportunities to develop new business.

There is a genuine sales element to the role, so you'll need to be comfortable picking up the phone, starting conversations and asking for the business. However, this isn't a traditional BDM position focused solely on cold acquisition or being out on the road.

Working within a small, close-knit team, you'll also be someone who is happy to jump in and assist with incoming calls and general client enquiries when needed.


Key Responsibilities
  • Proactively contact existing, previous and prospective clients to generate hire opportunities
  • Build and maintain relationships with clients across the civil and construction sectors
  • Re-engage dormant clients and identify upcoming projects or equipment requirements
  • Manage inbound hire enquiries via phone and email
  • Prepare quotes and proactively follow up outstanding opportunities
  • Identify and approach prospective clients where appropriate
  • Promote available equipment to maximise fleet utilisation
  • Maintain accurate client and sales activity within HubSpot CRM
  • Assist with incoming calls and general client enquiries across the office when required
  • Conduct phone and Microsoft Teams meetings, with occasional site visits where beneficial
  • Work closely with the wider team to maintain client engagement and sales momentum

About You
We're looking for someone who genuinely enjoys speaking with clients and is comfortable with the commercial side of relationship building.
You'll ideally be:
  • Confident making proactive outbound calls and asking clients about upcoming requirements
  • Personable, genuine and able to build rapport quickly
  • Commercially minded and comfortable identifying sales opportunities
  • Comfortable approaching new clients as well as working with established relationships
  • Persistent with follow-ups without being overly pushy
  • Reliable, consistent and willing to get involved wherever needed
  • Organised and disciplined with quotes, follow-ups and CRM activity
  • Comfortable working autonomously within a small office environment
  • Looking for a stable, long-term opportunity where you can become a valued part of the team

Experience within plant and equipment hire, earthmoving, civil construction, construction or a related industry will be highly regarded. Strong internal sales, hire or client relationship experience from another industry will also be considered.


What's on Offer
  • $80,000–$85,000 + super
  • Permanent, full-time opportunity
  • Dandenong South location
  • 100% office-based, with occasional site visits
  • Small, close-knit and down-to-earth team
  • Established client relationships to build upon
  • A varied mix of client relationships, hire coordination and proactive sales
  • Stable, long-term opportunity within an established business

job.title: Mine Operator
job.description:

Rio Tinto is a global mining and materials company operating in 35 countries, producing the materials essential to modern life. Their operations are built on safety, innovation, inclusion and creating value for communities, customers and shareholders. 
Through Rio Tinto’s partnership with Chandler Macleod, we are seeking multiple Entry Level Mine Operators to join the Northern Andoom Operations in Weipa. 
  • No previous mining experience required 
  • Full on-the-job training provided 
  • 4/5/5/4 rotating day/night roster

The 4/5/5/4 rotating day/night roster gives you the opportunity to build a career in mining while continuing to live and work locally in Weipa.

job.title: Document Controller
job.description:
Document Controller

Location: Booragoon, WA (Initial onboarding and training based in Pinjarra)
Rate: $50 - $55 per hour + Superannuation (Negotiable AND Highly dependent on experience)
Contract Duration: 12-month contract with strong potential for extension

We are seeking an experienced Document Controller with experience supporting engineering, mining, EPCM, construction or major capital projects. This role is focused on the management of engineering drawings, project documentation, transmittals and document management systems within a project delivery environment.

job.title: Senior Contract Manager
job.description:
Senior Contracts Manager
Melbourne CBD / Hybrid / $99ph + super
Short-Term 3 month contract - potential extension

We are seeking a seasoned Senior Contracts Manager to provide commercial leadership across a portfolio of complex infrastructure and project-related contracts.
This is a strategic role for an experienced contracts professional who can confidently operate across procurement, contract governance, commercial risk and stakeholder management.
Working closely with senior leaders and project teams, you will provide expert advice and oversight to ensure commercial outcomes are achieved while maintaining compliance with government procurement policies and contractual obligations.

As a senior member of the Commercial team, you will be responsible for leading contract management activities across a diverse portfolio of design, construction, goods and services contracts.
You will drive procurement and contracting strategies, oversee complex supplier relationships, manage commercial risk and provide high-level advice to stakeholders throughout the contract lifecycle.
This role requires a proactive leader who can balance operational delivery with strategic commercial decision-making.

Key Responsibilities
  • Provide strategic leadership and commercial oversight across complex project contracts.
  • Lead procurement planning, sourcing strategies and tender activities, including RFQ and RFT processes.
  • Drive best-practice contract management frameworks, governance and compliance.
  • Lead complex commercial negotiations and deliver value-for-money outcomes.
  • Identify, assess and mitigate contractual, operational and commercial risks.
  • Act as a trusted advisor to project delivery teams and senior stakeholders.
  • Manage supplier relationships, contract performance, variations and dispute resolution.
  • Oversee contract compliance, reporting and performance outcomes.
  • Partner with legal, finance, risk and project teams to ensure successful commercial outcomes.
  • Champion continuous improvement initiatives across procurement and contract management functions.
About You
You are a highly experienced commercial professional with a strong track record managing complex contracts within infrastructure, construction, transport, government or major project environments.

You will bring:
  • Tertiary qualifications in Business, Commerce, Law, Procurement, Supply Chain or a related discipline.
  • Significant experience in senior contract management, procurement or commercial leadership roles.
  • Demonstrated success managing complex construction, infrastructure or project-based contracts.
  • Extensive experience leading procurement activities and strategic sourcing initiatives.
  • Strong commercial acumen with the ability to negotiate and influence at a senior level.
  • Experience providing strategic procurement and contract advice to executive stakeholders.
  • Exceptional stakeholder engagement, communication and relationship management skills.
  • Government, rail, transport, infrastructure or construction sector experience will be highly regarded.

If you're an experienced Senior Contracts Manager looking to apply your commercial expertise within a major projects environment, we'd love to hear from you.

Please note that only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

job.title: Senior Quality Officer
job.description:
About the company:

This Federal Government agency works to deliver programs and services that support people with disability and their families, aiming to improve access, engagement, and outcomes across Australia. The agency collaborates closely with communities, service providers, and government stakeholders to implement initiatives that enhance social inclusion, wellbeing, and equity.

About the Team

The National Early Childhood team works closely with children and families to provide access to supports and services that make a meaningful difference. The team is committed to delivering high-quality, consistent, and sustainable planning outcomes through quality assurance, stakeholder engagement, and continuous improvement.


About the Role
As a Quality Officer, you will play a key role in reviewing and improving the quality of planning and decision-making processes. You will provide technical guidance, support staff capability, analyse trends and data, manage escalations, and contribute to quality improvement initiatives across the branch.
This role is ideal for someone who enjoys problem-solving, coaching others, analysing information, and driving better outcomes through quality and continuous improvement.

Key Responsibilities
 
  • Conduct quality assurance and quality control activities relating to early childhood planning and decision-making.
  • Provide technical advice and support on complex quality-related matters.
  • Coach and mentor team members to improve decision-making quality, technical capability, and consistency.
  • Analyse quality trends and performance data to identify risks and improvement opportunities.
  • Assist in developing and implementing continuous improvement initiatives.
  • Manage escalations and provide timely recommendations and resolutions.
  • Liaise with stakeholders to provide advice, education, and information on early childhood planning and quality practices.
  • Support compliance with legislation, policies, procedures, and quality standards.
  • Contribute to branch goals through effective reporting, analysis, and quality oversight.

You Must Have
 
  • Experience in quality assurance, compliance, auditing, planning, or operational quality functions.
  • Strong ability to interpret and apply legislation, policies, procedures, and standards.
  • Experience providing advice and support on complex operational or policy matters.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement and communication skills.
  • Proven ability to mentor, coach, and support others.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Advanced Excel and data analysis capabilities.
  • Ability to manage competing priorities and work with a high degree of autonomy.
  • Qualification in Allied Health, Education, Disability, or a related field.


Benefits:
  • ASAP start (pending Federal Police Clearance)
  • 12-month assignment with potential extension
  • Location:  National
  • $60.26 Hourly + Super


How to apply:

Chandler Macleod is an equal opportunity employer as part of our commitment to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, disability and culturally and linguistics candidates are also encouraged to apply.

Please note the successful candidate for the role must hold Australian Citizenship.



Application closes on the 16th of October 2026

Melbourne CBD | Hybrid (2-3 Days in Office)

We're seeking an experienced SharePoint Consultant to join a major digital transformation project focused on delivering a modern Microsoft 365-based intranet for a Victorian Government organisation.

Working within a project delivery team, you'll help design, configure and optimise a new intranet built on SharePoint Online (Modern Experience) and the broader Microsoft 365 platform.

  • Design and improve information architecture, metadata and content organisation
  • Support content migration and transition activities

  • Integrate SharePoint with Microsoft 365 applications including Teams, OneDrive and Power Platform
  • Collaborate with business stakeholders to understand requirements and deliver practical solutions

  • Strong stakeholder engagement and consulting skills
  • Excellent communication skills and the ability to translate business requirements into practical solutions

job.description:
Are you looking for meaningful, part-time work that fits seamlessly around your lifestyle and offers excellent work–life balance? If so, our School Crossing Supervisor role could be the perfect opportunity for you.

As a School Crossing Supervisor, you will play a vital role in keeping school-aged children, families, and pedestrians safe during busy morning and afternoon school times. This is a rewarding position where you’ll become a familiar and trusted face in your local community.

  • Assist children and pedestrians to safely cross the road during peak school hours

  • Be friendly, reliable, community-minded, and confident communicating with people of all ages

  • Accrual of Annual Leave and Sick/Carer’s Leave

job.description:
Are you an experienced Document Controller looking to contribute to major construction and energy infrastructure projects? Our client AGL is seeking a highly organised Document Controller to support the successful delivery of construction projects across Western Australia. Based in Perth, this 12-month contract opportunity offers the chance to work within a project-focused environment, in a hybrid working environment ensuring critical project documentation is managed, maintained, and governed throughout the construction lifecycle. 

This role will involve occasional travel to project sites in WA and interaction with a wide range of stakeholders including project teams, contractors, and operations personnel.

About the Role
Working within the Construction Management Office, you will play a key role in ensuring project information is accurate, accessible, secure, and compliant with established governance requirements. You will support project teams by administering document control processes, maintaining project information systems, and facilitating smooth information handover to operational teams.

Key Responsibilities
  • Manage and maintain project documentation, records, and information throughout the project lifecycle.

  • Opportunity working at Rio Tinto
  • Ongoing assignment via Chandler Macleod

About the Opportunity
Rio Tinto is a global mining and materials company operating in 35 countries, producing the materials essential to modern life. Their operations are built on safety, innovation, inclusion and creating value for communities, customers and shareholders. 
Through Rio Tinto’s partnership with Chandler Macleod, we are seeking an experienced Master Data Specialist - Fixed Plant.

The Master Data Specialist is responsible for maintaining and improving the integrity, accuracy, and governance of Fixed Plant asset master data across SAP, ALIM, engineering drawings and associated business systems. The role ensures alignment of asset information including Functional Locations (FLOCs), Bills of Materials (BOMs), equipment records, maintenance plans, tactics, and engineering documentation to support safe, reliable and efficient maintenance execution.
Flexible roster arrangements can be provided for this role. Flexibility to attend site for shutdowns when required, typically every 6-13 weeks, is desirable.
Reporting to the Superintendent Planning & Engineering and working in a collaborative environment across Engineering, Maintenance, Planning and Reliability, you will:

  • Create, modify and maintain Functional Locations (FLOCs), Equipment Records and Bills of Materials (BOMs)
  • Maintain Maintenance Plans, Task Lists, Measurement Points and Spare Parts Structures
  • Contribute to the integrity and accuracy of asset data across SAP, ALIM and engineering documentation
  • Work safely within Rio Tinto procedures
About You
  • Engineering qualification, Mechanical Trade or Electrical Trade qualification
  • Genuine in-field experience working with Fixed Plant / Wet Plant equipment
  • Experience with SAP PM and Fixed Plant asset master data
  • Knowledge of Functional Locations (FLOCs), Bills of Materials (BOMs), equipment records and asset hierarchies
  • Strong stakeholder engagement skills with the ability to work across Engineering, Maintenance, Planning, Reliability and Operations
  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to accurate asset data
  • Flexibility to attend site for shutdowns when required, typically every 6-13 weeks
  • Ability to pass pre-employment medical and other testing

Chandler Macleod is one of Australia’s most experienced workforce partners. job.title: HR Specialists & Talent Advisors - Multiple 6 month opportunities
job.description:
Multiple 6-Month Temporary Opportunities | Level 4 & Level 6 | Public Sector

Are you an experienced HR professional looking to contribute to high-profile workforce projects within a public sector environment?
We are seeking talented HR practitioners to join a specialist People & Culture team for six-month temporary assignments. These opportunities will suit professionals with experience in job evaluation and classification, senior executive employment arrangements, or talent acquisition and recruitment.
With multiple vacancies available across several HR disciplines, this is an excellent opportunity to apply your expertise in a collaborative and fast-paced environment.

Available Opportunities

HR Specialist - Classification & Job Evaluation (Level 6)

We are seeking an experienced HR professional with demonstrated expertise in position classification and work value assessment, ideally within the WA public sector or a comparable government environment.
Key responsibilities include:
  • Reviewing and assessing Job Description Forms (JDFs)
  • Conducting job classification and work value assessments
  • Providing clear, evidence-based classification advice
  • Preparing supporting documentation and recommendations
  • Contributing to organisational workforce and position management initiatives
Experience applying the BIPERS job evaluation methodology will be highly regarded.

HR Specialist - Senior Executive Service Support (Level 6)

This role will support senior executive employment and classification activities within a government setting.
Key responsibilities include:
  • Undertaking Senior Executive Service (SES) classification assessments
  • Preparing classification and appointment business cases
  • Coordinating submissions to relevant government authorities
  • Supporting SES recruitment and appointment processes
  • Providing advice on executive employment arrangements and frameworks
Applicants with previous experience supporting SES or equivalent executive employment arrangements are encouraged to apply.

Talent Advisors (2 Positions Available) - Level 4

We are seeking proactive recruitment professionals to support end-to-end talent acquisition activities.
Working closely with hiring managers and stakeholders, you will play a key role in attracting, sourcing and securing high-quality talent across a diverse range of positions.
Responsibilities may include:
  • Managing recruitment and selection processes
  • Providing advice on recruitment policies and procedures
  • Drafting and advertising vacancies
  • Coordinating assessments, interviews and appointment processes
  • Building strong relationships with hiring managers and candidates
  • Supporting workforce planning and talent attraction initiatives
About You

To be successful, you will demonstrate:
  • Relevant HR, recruitment, workforce or organisational development experience
  • Strong communication and stakeholder engagement skills
  • The ability to manage competing priorities and deliver quality outcomes
  • Sound analytical, report writing and problem-solving capabilities
  • Experience within the WA public sector or government environment will be highly regarded
What's on Offer?
  • Multiple six-month temporary opportunities
  • Attractive public sector remuneration
  • Opportunity to contribute to significant workforce projects
  • Collaborative and supportive team environment
  • Valuable experience within a large and complex organisation
Whether your expertise lies in classification and job evaluation, senior executive employment, or talent acquisition, we welcome applications from experienced HR professionals looking to make an immediate impact.

This senior leadership opportunity will see you driving engagement strategies, managing complex stakeholder relationships, leading a high-performing team, and ensuring community feedback is effectively integrated into project planning and delivery. Reporting to the General Manager, Project Communication, you will provide strategic leadership across communication and engagement activities within a designated project region. job.title: Project Manager (Specialist Projects)
job.description:
Project Manager (Specialist Projects)
Kurri Kurri, NSW
Attractive Salary Package

Our client is seeking an experienced and results-driven Project Manager to join their Project Delivery team based in Kurri Kurri, NSW.

This is an exciting opportunity to lead a diverse portfolio of sustaining and capital projects across mobile delivery systems, infrastructure upgrades, commissioning activities, asset mobilisation, and operational improvement initiatives.

About the Role Reporting to the Lead Projects, you will be responsible for the end-to-end delivery of multiple projects, ensuring outcomes are achieved safely, on time, within budget, and to the highest standards.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Managing multiple sustaining and capital projects simultaneously.
  • Developing project scopes, schedules, budgets, and risk management plans.
  • Coordinating contractors, suppliers, procurement activities, and project resources.
  • Managing project governance, reporting, forecasting, and project controls.
  • Leading mobilisation, construction, commissioning, and handover activities.
  • Building strong relationships with internal and external stakeholders.
  • Ensuring compliance with safety, environmental, and regulatory requirements.
  • Driving projects through to successful completion while balancing competing priorities.
About You
We are looking for a practical project professional with a strong delivery focus and the ability to navigate complexity.

You may come from a background in:
  • Project Delivery
  • Mining
  • Fixed Plant or Mobile Equipment
  • Civil Construction
  • Heavy Manufacturing
  • Maintenance and Shutdowns
  • Operations or Logistics
  • Trades or Construction Supervision
While engineering qualifications may be beneficial, this is not a design engineering role. We are particularly interested in candidates who have successfully coordinated and delivered projects within operational, maintenance, construction, or manufacturing environments. Formal project management qualifications will be highly regarded.

What Will Make You Successful

The ideal candidate will:
  • Make sound decisions with incomplete information.
  • Thrive in ambiguous and changing environments.
  • Balance competing stakeholder expectations.
  • Drive outcomes despite uncertainty.
  • Maintain strong ownership and accountability.
  • Be highly organised and capable of managing multiple projects concurrently.
  • Hold stakeholders accountable and follow through on commitments.
  • Focus on delivering practical outcomes rather than pursuing technical perfection.
In short, we're looking for someone who can bring structure to complexity, coordinate multiple stakeholders, and consistently deliver successful project outcomes.

Key Requirements
  • 5+ years' experience managing capital and/or sustaining projects.
  • Qualifications in Project Management, Engineering, Construction, or equivalent industry experience.
  • Strong contractor management and stakeholder engagement skills.
  • Demonstrated experience managing project budgets, schedules, and risk.
  • Excellent communication, planning, and organisational skills.
  • Experience working within industrial, manufacturing, mining, maintenance, or construction environments.
What's on Offer
  • Attractive salary package.
  • Opportunity to manage a diverse portfolio of projects with significant business impact.
  • Supportive and collaborative project delivery environment.
  • Minimal travel requirements (less than 10%).
  • Based in Kurri Kurri, NSW.
If you're a proactive Project Manager who enjoys creating order from complexity, influencing stakeholders, and delivering outcomes, we'd love to hear from you. Apply today for a confidential discussion.

At Chandler Macleod, we are committed to fostering a diverse workforce where everyone is welcome. We encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, women, neurodiverse, people living with a disability and the LGBTIQA+ community.

You can read more about our commitment to diversity and inclusion at https://www.chandlermacleod.com/diversity-and-inclusion.

job.title: Safety Advisor
job.description:
Safety Advisor | Construction

$966 per day inclusive of super | Truganina
Initial 12-month contract | Long-term opportunity through to April 2028
Full-time | 3 days per week onsite

We are seeking an experienced Safety Advisor to provide dedicated health and safety assurance across a large-scale construction and operational environment in Truganina.

This role will work across a complex multi-contractor site, providing safety advice, assurance and oversight during construction activities that interface with operational teams. You’ll partner closely with internal safety and project stakeholders, the Principal Contractor, subcontractors and site leadership to support safe work practices and strong safety outcomes.

Importantly, this is an assurance and advisory role. It does not replace or assume the safety management responsibilities of the Principal Contractor or other employers undertaking work onsite.

The role
You will be responsible for:
  • Conducting site inspections, audits and spot checks across construction and operational activities
  • Monitoring high-risk construction activities and escalating safety concerns where required
  • Reviewing and verifying SWMS, permits and other relevant safety documentation
  • Providing advice on construction risk management and safe work practices
  • Supporting the implementation and adoption of OHS systems and processes
  • Identifying existing and emerging hazards and supporting corrective and preventative actions
  • Supporting incident investigations, inspections and reporting
  • Monitoring corrective actions and ensuring appropriate follow-through
  • Working closely with project, automation, safety, contractor and site leadership teams
  • Supporting safety initiatives and continual improvement activities
  • Coaching and influencing contractors, leaders and operational teams to strengthen safety behaviours
  • Supporting OHS compliance, reporting, data analysis and performance tracking
  • Preparing safety reports, metrics and KPIs for leadership and project stakeholders
  • Liaising with regulators and external stakeholders where required
  • Attending toolbox talks and site meetings as required
About youTo be successful, you will ideally bring:
  • Previous experience as an OHS / Safety Advisor within construction, major projects or another high-risk environment
  • Strong experience working across multi-contractor construction sites
  • A background in contractor safety management and safety assurance
  • Strong knowledge of Victorian OHS legislation, regulatory requirements and industry standards
  • Experience reviewing SWMS and other high-risk construction documentation
  • Experience supporting incident investigations and corrective actions
  • Confidence engaging with contractors, supervisors, site managers and senior stakeholders
  • Strong coaching, influencing and relationship-building skills
  • The ability to work independently, identify issues and proactively drive outcomes
  • Strong reporting, documentation and Microsoft Office skills

Qualifications
Ideally you will hold:
  • Certificate IV in Work Health and Safety or higher
  • ICAM investigation training or similar
  • Current Construction White Card
  • Current CPR and First Aid qualifications

The details
  • Rate: $966 per day inclusive of super
  • Location: Truganina, VIC
  • Contract: Initial 12 months, with the approved project duration currently extending to approximately April 2028
  • Hours: Full-time, with site operating hours generally between 6:00am and 4:00pm
  • Onsite requirement: Approximately 3 days per week onsite
  • Large-scale construction environment with significant contractor and operational interfaces

This is a strong opportunity for an experienced construction safety professional who enjoys being visible onsite, working collaboratively with multiple stakeholders and providing practical, credible safety assurance across a complex project environment.

job.title: Branch Manager
job.description:
Branch Manager | Canberra | FMCG & Distribution

Permanent | Full time

$165,000 – $175,000 + super | STI | Fully Maintained Company Vehicle
  • Senior leadership opportunity within a well-established national business
  • Lead a 50–60 person branch operation
  • Responsibility across sales, operations, transport, warehouse and customer service
  • Potential relocation assistance for the right candidate
The Opportunity

We are seeking an experienced Branch Manager to take overall responsibility for a large and established distribution operation in Canberra.

This is a senior leadership position with responsibility across sales, operations, transport, warehouse, administration and customer service, with a strong focus on branch profitability, customer service and team performance.

Reporting to senior management, you'll lead a team of approximately 50–60 employees and work closely with an experienced leadership group across the branch.

This is an opportunity for a confident and commercially minded leader to take ownership of an established operation, drive performance and identify opportunities to improve the way the business operates.

About the Role

You'll be responsible for:
  • Leading the day-to-day operations of the branch across sales, warehouse, transport and administration.
  • Delivering budgeted EBIT, revenue and profitability targets.
  • Managing branch budgets, forecasts, costs and financial performance.
  • Analysing P&L results and operational KPIs and taking corrective action where required.
  • Leading and developing a team of approximately 50–60 employees.
  • Driving customer growth, retention and service excellence.
  • Building strong relationships with customers, suppliers and internal stakeholders.
  • Managing inventory and ensuring customer demand is supported effectively.
  • Identifying new business opportunities and opportunities for growth.
  • Improving productivity, processes and operational efficiency.
  • Ensuring high standards of WHS, food safety, HACCP and Chain of Responsibility compliance.
  • Creating a culture of accountability, teamwork and continuous improvement.
  • Making timely decisions and providing clear direction across the branch.
About You

We're looking for an experienced operational leader who combines commercial understanding with strong people and operational leadership.

You'll ideally have:
  • Previous experience as a Branch Manager, Operations Manager, Distribution Manager, General Manager or similar.
  • Experience managing a sizeable workforce and multiple operational functions.
  • Strong commercial acumen and the ability to interpret P&L, budgets and financial performance.
  • Experience managing costs, productivity and operational KPIs.
  • Strong customer relationship and stakeholder management skills.
  • Excellent problem-solving and decision-making ability.
  • A visible, hands-on leadership style.
  • The confidence to challenge existing processes and drive positive change.
  • Strong communication and people management skills.
  • The ability to perform in a fast-paced, operational environment.
Experience in these areas will be highly regarded:
  • FMCG
  • Food distribution or foodservice
  • Grocery or wholesale distribution
  • Transport and logistics
  • Warehouse and distribution
  • High-volume operational environments
  • HACCP and food safety
  • Chain of Responsibility
  • WHS and psychosocial safety
Forklift or heavy vehicle licences are advantageous but not essential.

The Leadership Opportunity

This role will suit someone who enjoys being close to the operation and isn't afraid to make decisions.

You'll be taking over an established operation with experienced people and established ways of working.

The opportunity is to build on what's working, identify what can be improved and lead the team through positive change.

We're looking for someone who:
  • Takes ownership
  • Leads from the front
  • Makes decisions
  • Holds people accountable
  • Develops and supports their team
  • Builds strong customer relationships
  • Looks for better ways of doing things
  • Can balance people, customers and commercial outcomes
What's on Offer
  • $165,000 – $175,000 + super
  • Fully maintained company vehicle
  • STI / incentive program
  • Potential relocation assistance for the right candidate
  • Staff discounts and additional benefits
  • Opportunity to lead a substantial operation within an established national business
  • Genuine scope to influence operational performance and branch growth
Apply Now

If you're an experienced Branch or Operations Manager looking for a role where you can take genuine ownership and make a measurable impact, we'd like to hear from you.

Apply now with your updated resume and cover letter.

Early applications are encouraged, as shortlisting may commence before the closing date of Friday 2 October 2026.

Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. All applications will be treated confidentially.

As part of the recruitment process, successful candidates may be required to complete employment checks, which may include a medical assessment, drug and alcohol testing, National Police History Check and licence validation.

This senior leadership opportunity will see you driving engagement strategies, managing complex stakeholder relationships, leading a high-performing team, and ensuring community feedback is effectively integrated into project planning and delivery. About the Role
Reporting to the General Manager, Project Communication, you will provide strategic leadership across communication and engagement activities within a designated project region. You will oversee engagement programs, manage sensitive stakeholder matters, and guide teams through complex community, property and construction-related issues.
This role requires a highly experienced communications professional who can operate confidently in politically sensitive environments while delivering outstanding stakeholder outcomes.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead the development and execution of communication and community engagement strategies aligned to organisational objectives.

  • Develop innovative communication initiatives that foster transparency and trust.

Project Delivery & Reporting
  • Monitor stakeholder sentiment, emerging risks and community concerns.

  • Oversee engagement data collection, analysis and reporting.
  • Ensure engagement activities comply with legislative, regulatory and policy requirements.
  • Support procurement and administrative activities as required.

About You
To be successful, you will bring:
  • Extensive experience (10+ years) in community engagement, stakeholder relations, public affairs or communications leadership roles.
  • Demonstrated success delivering engagement strategies for major infrastructure, government or large-scale projects.
  • Experience managing complex stakeholder environments, including planning approvals, property acquisition, construction impacts and community issues.
  • Proven ability to lead high-performing teams and foster collaborative workplace cultures.
  • Strong strategic communications, negotiation and conflict resolution skills.
  • Experience preparing executive briefings, reports and strategic recommendations.

job.description:
Warehouse Worker with Amazon
  • Work at Amazon Australia’s Fulfilment Centre located in Cranbourne West
  • Employee parking available onsite
  • Training and ongoing support provided
  • Flexible work across day and night shifts
Your starting rate of pay is $32.64, with rates of pay for any day you operate a forklift startng at $37.74 and you get paid penalties if you work night, early morning or weekend shifts.

This is a casual role where you will be required to be available across 4 days per week (including 1 day on the weekend). We have day and night shifts available with each shift being 10 hours long. Experience is not required for these positions and full onsite training is provided.

  • Must have a valid forklift licence

In return Amazon offers a safe, inclusive and fun environment to set you up for success so you can work hard, have fun and make history.

job.title: Workers Compensation Consultant Level 5
job.description:
Workers Compensation Consultant (Level 5)

6-Month Temporary Contract | Part-Time (3-4 Days per Week) | Hybrid Working Arrangement

Are you an experienced Workers Compensation and Injury Management professional looking for a flexible opportunity within State Government? This is your chance to join our client based in Joondalup and play a key role in supporting employee wellbeing and organisational capability through effective workers compensation and injury management practices.

About the Role

We are seeking a skilled Workers Compensation Consultant (Level 5) to join the team on a six-month temporary contract. Working 3-4 days per week (7.5 hours per day), this position offers a flexible hybrid arrangement, combining work from home with time spent in the Joondalup office.
Reporting within the People and Capability function, you will provide specialist advice and coordinate workers compensation and injury management activities across the organisation. This is an excellent opportunity to apply your expertise while contributing to the development of improved injury management frameworks and practices.

Key Responsibilities
  • Manage and process workers compensation claims from lodgement through to resolution.
  • Coordinate and support non-compensable employees returning to work following illness or injury.
  • Assess and evaluate organisational requirements relating to both compensable and non-compensable injuries and illnesses.
  • Provide timely advice and support to managers, employees and key stakeholders on workers compensation and injury management matters.
  • Develop and maintain productive relationships with insurers, medical practitioners and other external stakeholders.
  • Contribute to the development of a contemporary framework to support the effective management of workplace injuries and illnesses across the organisation.
  • Ensure compliance with relevant legislation, policies and procedures while maintaining accurate case records.
About You

To be successful in this role, you will demonstrate:
  • Proven experience in workers compensation claims management and injury management.
  • Sound knowledge of return-to-work and rehabilitation principles.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement and relationship management skills.
  • The ability to provide practical, accurate advice while managing a diverse caseload.
  • Excellent communication, organisational and problem-solving abilities.
  • Experience working within a government or large organisational environment will be highly regarded.
What's on Offer?
  • Level 5 State Government contract opportunity
  • Six-month temporary assignment
  • Flexible part-time hours (3-4 days per week)
  • Hybrid work arrangement with work-from-home flexibility and Joondalup office attendance

The Audit and Assurance Officer plays a key role in supporting the agency's governance, audit, assurance, risk management, and business continuity functions.
Working closely with internal stakeholders, service providers, and governance committees, you will coordinate internal audits, monitor audit recommendations, support risk and assurance activities, and contribute to the ongoing improvement of governance and risk frameworks. You will also assist in strengthening organisational resilience through the management and coordination of business continuity planning and testing activities.

job.title: Senior Project Manager (Civil Construction)
job.description:
Permanent | Cairns | Senior Project Leadership | Civil Construction


For an experienced civil Project Manager, this is an opportunity to take genuine ownership of project delivery, with responsibility extending well beyond programme management and reporting.

Based in Cairns, this permanent Senior Project Manager position sits within an established civil construction business delivering a diverse range of infrastructure projects.

This isn't a role sitting several layers removed from construction. You'll have overall responsibility for the project and its performance, leading the delivery team while maintaining oversight across commercial, programme, quality, safety, client and construction outcomes.

You'll be supported by an experienced engineering and quality team, including Project Engineers, Site Engineers and quality resources. The expectation is that you'll provide the leadership, direction and commercial oversight needed to keep projects performing from mobilisation through to completion.


What you'll be responsible for:


Your remit will cover the full lifecycle of civil construction projects, including:
  • Taking overall responsibility for project delivery from mobilisation through to completion
  • Leading Project Engineers, Site Engineers, supervisors, subcontractors and project support resources
  • Managing project budgets, forecasting, cost performance and overall commercial outcomes
  • Developing and driving construction programmes and ensuring key milestones are achieved
  • Managing procurement, subcontractors, variations and contractual requirements
  • Maintaining strong standards across safety, quality, compliance and project risk
  • Building effective relationships with clients, stakeholders and delivery partners
  • Providing practical leadership and direction to resolve issues and keep projects moving
  • Taking accountability for the performance of both the project and the team delivering it

Who we're looking for:


We're looking for someone who has built their career close to civil construction delivery and understands what it means to have genuine accountability for the whole project.

This will particularly suit someone experienced in a regional or mid-sized civil contractor environment, where Project Managers are expected to understand the commercial detail, know what's happening on site, lead their teams and take ownership of the final outcome.


To be considered, you'll need to bring:
  • A Degree in Civil Engineering (highly regarded)
  • Substantial experience in civil construction, with ideally five or more years operating at Project Manager level
  • A strong contractor-side background delivering civil infrastructure projects
  • Demonstrated experience taking projects from planning and mobilisation through construction to completion
  • Strong commercial capability across budgets, forecasting, procurement, contracts and cost control
  • Experience leading engineering, construction and subcontractor teams
  • A practical understanding of civil construction methodology, quality, safety and project risk
  • The judgement and leadership capability to make decisions, solve problems and remain accountable for project outcomes


Why consider the opportunity?


If you're looking for a role where you can have genuine influence over how projects are run, this is an opportunity to take ownership without being lost within a large corporate project structure.
You'll be close enough to the work to understand what's happening on site while having the autonomy and support to lead the broader project, team and commercial outcomes.


The opportunity offers:
  • A permanent Senior Project Manager position based in Cairns
  • Genuine end-to-end ownership of civil construction projects
  • Dedicated engineering and quality support
  • A hands-on leadership role with direct influence over project performance
  • An established civil construction environment where experienced Project Managers are trusted to lead
  • Exposure to a diverse range of civil infrastructure projects
This could particularly suit an experienced Senior Project Manager or Project Manager who has built a career within civil contracting and is ready for broader responsibility across projects, people and commercial performance.


If your experience aligns and you'd like a confidential discussion about the position, projects, package and opportunity to establish yourself in Cairns, apply now or contact Anna Dziopa at Chandler Macleod on 07 2140 6649.

job.title: Force Design & Strategy Support Specialist
job.description:
About the company:

This Federal Government agency is responsible for protecting and advancing national security interests through the management of defence policy, strategy, and operations. It oversees the development and delivery of complex defence capabilities, including advanced maritime, land, and aerospace programs, while coordinating with domestic and international partners.

Delivery project Support Officer– 12-Month Assignment with potential extension
Location: Canberra ACT
Security Clearance: Minimum NV1

About the Team
The Land Command, Control, Communications and Computing (Land C4) Program and the Land Intelligence, Surveillance, Reconnaissance and Electronic Warfare (LISREW) Program sit within the LC4ISREW Directorate of Army Headquarters.
These programs are responsible for delivering and sustaining critical command, control, communications, intelligence, surveillance, reconnaissance and electronic warfare capabilities that enable situational awareness, information superiority and informed decision-making across the Agency.
Working within the Capability Management Office (CMO), you will support strategic planning, governance, capability development, and force design activities that contribute to Army's future capability and integrated force objectives.

About the Role
An exciting opportunity exists for an experienced Force Design and Strategy Support Specialist to support the Director LC4ISREW in strategic planning, force design, capability integration and future capability development activities.
You will play a key role in analysing strategic guidance, assessing capability dependencies, supporting force design initiatives, and providing high-quality advice that informs future Army and Defence capability decisions.
This position is ideal for someone with Defence capability, force design, systems integration, communications, ICT, or strategic planning experience who enjoys working in a highly collaborative and fast-paced Defence environment.

Responsibilities
 
  • Support the development and maintenance of LC4ISREW strategic plans and operational planning products.
  • Assist in the development of concepts of operation, concepts of employment and capability planning documentation.
  • Analyse Defence strategic guidance and assess impacts on future Land capability requirements.
  • Provide force design and strategic analysis to support informed capability planning and decision-making.
  • Review and coordinate capability planning activities across multiple Defence programs and capability streams.
  • Monitor and analyse dependencies between Land, Joint, Air Force, Navy and Defence projects.
  • Prepare strategic briefs, reports, presentations and recommendations for senior Defence stakeholders.
  • Support governance, planning and stakeholder engagement activities across Army Headquarters.
  • Assist in translating complex technical and military information into clear strategic advice.
  • Contribute to capability lifecycle planning, investment decisions and future force design initiatives.

You Must Have
  • Demonstrated experience supporting Defence programs, force design, capability development or strategic planning activities.
  • Strong understanding of Defence capability, communications systems, information systems, or integrated capability environments.
  • Excellent written communication skills, including experience preparing strategic documents, reports and briefings.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement skills and ability to work with military, APS and industry stakeholders.
  • Experience analysing complex information and providing strategic recommendations.
  • Excellent organisational skills with the ability to manage competing priorities.
  • Advanced Microsoft Office skills, including Word, Excel and PowerPoint.
  • Working knowledge of Microsoft Project.
  • Ability to interpret technical and operational information and communicate it clearly to diverse audiences.


How to apply:

Chandler Macleod is an equal opportunity employer as part of our commitment to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, disability and culturally and linguistics candidates are also encouraged to apply.

job.title: Transfer Station Operator
job.description:
About the role
We’re seeking a reliable Transfer Station Operator to support day-to-day operations at a busy Resource Recovery/Waste Management Centre in Ballina. You’ll be the first point of contact for visitors, providing helpful, calm customer service while directing vehicles and customers to the correct drop-off areas and encouraging safe, compliant recycling and resource recovery. The role also includes hands-on site support such as general labouring and grounds maintenance (e.g., litter collection, mowing/weeding and basic upkeep), completing standard paperwork (timesheets, work orders and WHS documentation), and working safely in line with site procedures.

Working hours are a key part of this role: you’ll work 7:30am–4:30pm on a rotating roster, starting 2–3 days per week with the potential to increase to full-time hours in early 2027. You must be available Monday to Friday and also commit to at least one weekend day (Saturday or Sunday) per fortnight—regular weekend work is required.


Duties
  • Provide friendly, professional customer service to waste centre visitors
  • Direct traffic and customers to the correct drop-off areas
  • Promote resource recovery and recycling by guiding correct sorting
  • Communicate load contents and details to the weighbridge operator
  • Advise customers on accepted vs non-accepted waste materials
  • Complete physically demanding outdoor work while following site safety requirements

Skills and Experience
  • Strong customer service and communication skills (confident dealing with the public)
  • Previous experience in physical, hands-on labouring work
  • Ability to follow procedures and communicate requirements clearly to customers
  • Strong work ethic, reliability, and initiative
  • Hepatitis A and B immunisation (required , or willingness to obtain)

Desirable:
  • Forklift ticket and practical operating experience
  • Waste management / transfer station / resource recovery experience
  • FEL tickets & white card 

Benefits
  • Strong weekend rates (Saturday $49 + super and Sunday $63 + super)
  • Consistent daytime hours (7:30am–4:30pm)
  • Opportunity to increase to full-time hours in early 2027 (performance and site needs dependent)

How to apply
Sound interesting? We would love to hear from you! Click APPLY NOW to upload a copy of your current resume & cover letter, or call Neva Niland on 02 6691 9101  for a confidential discussion.
