Are you a driven sales professional with experience selling construction materials into the commercial building sector? Do you thrive on building relationships with architects, builders, and key stakeholders, while managing projects from specification through to sale?

Our client is a well-established and growing Australian business supplying premium aluminium façade and architectural systems to the construction industry. Due to continued growth, they are seeking an ambitious Business Development Manager to drive sales, expand market share, and contribute to their long-term success.

Location Shepparton, VIC

Employment Type Full-Time, Permanent

Work Arrangement This role can be based remotely, with fortnightly travel to the Shepparton office. Regular state-wide travel will be required to meet with customers, architects, builders, and industry stakeholders.

About the Opportunity Reporting into the leadership team, you will be responsible for identifying and developing new business opportunities, managing an existing sales pipeline, and building strong relationships across the construction sector.

The successful candidate will play a key role in growing market presence and securing project specifications with architects and builders throughout a designated territory.

With a healthy pipeline of active and pending projects already in place, you'll be responsible for maintaining momentum, converting opportunities into sales, and expanding business growth.

Key Responsibilities
  • Develop and maintain relationships with architects, builders, developers, and contractors.
  • Secure project specifications and manage opportunities through the full sales cycle.
  • Maintain and grow a strong pipeline of sales opportunities.
  • Conduct regular client meetings and site visits across your territory.
  • Collaborate with estimating and marketing teams to generate quality leads.
  • Utilise CRM systems to manage opportunities, record activity, and track performance.
  • Monitor and maintain pipeline accuracy and reporting.
  • Work closely with internal stakeholders to achieve sales and growth targets.
  • Stay informed on construction industry trends, façade systems, and architectural products.
  • Deliver exceptional customer service and contribute to long-term client retention.
About You We're looking for someone who is commercially minded, self-motivated, and passionate about sales.

Essential Requirements
  • Minimum 2 years' experience selling construction materials in a B2B environment.
  • Proven experience dealing with architects, builders, and construction stakeholders.
  • Strong understanding of the construction industry.
  • Experience using CRM systems and working to weekly KPIs.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage a sales pipeline and drive results.
  • Excellent communication, negotiation, and relationship-building skills.
  • Highly motivated, resilient, and target-driven.
  • Willingness to undertake administrative tasks as part of a small and agile team environment.
  • Current driver's licence.
Desirable Qualifications & Experience
  • Qualifications in Building Design, Architecture, Construction Management, or a related field.
  • Experience with architectural façade systems or building products.
  • Ability to read and interpret construction drawings.
  • Experience with specification sales.
What We're Looking For The ideal candidate will embody the qualities of being:

  • Hungry – driven to succeed and exceed targets.
  • Humble – collaborative and willing to support the wider team.
  • Smart – commercially aware with strong interpersonal skills.
You'll be someone who enjoys building relationships, creating opportunities, and taking ownership of your results.

Salary & Benefits
  • Base salary of $110,000 + Super
  • Uncapped commission and bonus structure
  • Laptop and mobile phone provided
  • Opportunity to work with an established and growing business
  • Long-term career development potential
  • Autonomy and flexibility in managing your territory
Apply Now If you're an experienced construction sales professional looking for your next challenge and are motivated by building relationships, winning projects, and earning uncapped commissions, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply today or contact Chandler Macleod for a confidential discussion.

This Federal Government agency works to deliver programs and services that support people with disability and their families, aiming to improve access, engagement, and outcomes across Australia. The agency collaborates closely with communities, service providers, and government stakeholders to implement initiatives that enhance social inclusion, wellbeing, and equity.

About the Team

The team plays a critical role in supporting the agency's risk and integrity functions through advanced data analysis, reporting, and evidence-based insights. Working in a highly collaborative environment, the team partners with stakeholders across business areas to identify trends, manage risks, improve decision-making, and support strategic priorities. Team members contribute to complex projects that help drive operational excellence and deliver meaningful outcomes for Australians.

About the Role
An exciting opportunity exists for an experienced Data Analyst to join the agency. This role requires a highly capable professional who can work independently on complex analytical activities, provide strategic insights, and support decision-making through data-driven recommendations.
The successful candidate will undertake detailed analytical work, manage competing priorities, and contribute to projects that influence both operational and strategic outcomes. You will collaborate with a wide range of stakeholders, present findings to diverse audiences, and provide guidance to junior team members.
This is an excellent opportunity for someone who enjoys solving complex problems, working with large datasets, and translating data into meaningful insights that drive organisational outcomes.


Key Responsibilities
  • Conduct complex data analysis, reporting, and investigative activities to support business objectives.
  • Manage day-to-day analytical tasks, including regular reporting, project work, and ad hoc requests.
  • Analyse large and complex datasets to identify trends, risks, opportunities, and business insights.
  • Develop and maintain reports, dashboards, and performance metrics.
  • Contribute to reporting governance, quality assurance, and data integrity processes.
  • Interpret analytical findings and provide evidence-based recommendations to stakeholders.
  • Collaborate with teams across the agency to ensure consistent data usage, reporting, and messaging.
  • Present analytical outcomes and insights to both technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Support stakeholder engagement and build strong internal and external relationships.
  • Mentor and develop junior analysts, promoting best practices in data analysis and reporting.
  • Support project delivery and contribute to strategic initiatives within the risk and integrity functions.

You Must Have
 
  • Strong experience in data analytics and data interpretation.
  • Advanced SQL skills and experience working with large datasets.
  • Experience using analytics and reporting tools, ideally SAS Enterprise Guide (SAS EG) and/or SAS Viya.
  • Strong problem-solving skills with the ability to identify and resolve complex data-related issues.
  • Excellent critical thinking capabilities and the ability to make evidence-based decisions.
  • Strong communication skills, including the ability to explain complex data insights to both technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Proven ability to build productive stakeholder relationships and collaborate across multidisciplinary teams.
  • Experience preparing reports, presentations, and briefing materials for senior stakeholders.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities and work effectively with a high degree of autonomy.
  • Experience with Python and/or R programming languages.
  • Knowledge of statistical analysis and machine learning techniques.
  • Experience in fraud analytics, risk analytics, or integrity-related environments.
  • Experience working within a large and complex government or regulated environment.


Benefits:
  • ASAP start (pending Federal Police Clearance)
  • 12-month assignment with potential extension
  • Location:  Deakin ACT, Richmond VIC, Geelong VIC, Chermside QLD, Surry Hills NSW, Newcastle NSW


How to apply:

Chandler Macleod is an equal opportunity employer as part of our commitment to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, disability and culturally and linguistics candidates are also encouraged to apply.

Please note the successful candidate for the role must hold Australian Citizenship.

job.title: Plant Operator

As a Plant Operator, you will play a key role in the safe and efficient operation of the rendering facility. You will be responsible for monitoring production processes, operating plant equipment, conducting routine checks, and maintaining high standards of safety, quality, and hygiene.

We are looking for dependable individuals who enjoy hands-on work and thrive in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.

job.title: Senior Cyber Security Advisor
job.description:
Are you an experienced Cyber Security professional with a strong advisory background and expertise supporting complex, highly regulated environments?

We are seeking a Senior Cyber Security Advisor to join our client AGL on a contract basis. This is a strategic role responsible for providing expert cyber security guidance across business and technology initiatives, helping strengthen cyber resilience and protect critical infrastructure against an evolving threat landscape. This is an initial six month contract, based in Melbourne in a hybrid working environment.

Working closely with senior stakeholders across business and technology teams, you will play a key role in identifying, assessing and managing cyber security risks while ensuring compliance with industry standards, regulatory requirements and organisational policies.

About the Role

As a trusted cyber security partner, you will provide strategic advice and leadership across a broad range of initiatives, ensuring security considerations are embedded into decision-making, transformation programs and operational activities.

Key responsibilities include:
  • Provide expert cyber security advice across strategic and operational initiatives.
  • Identify, assess and manage cyber security risks across technology and business projects.
  • Partner with business leaders, technology teams, subsidiaries, vendors and external stakeholders to strengthen cyber security outcomes.
  • Develop, implement and maintain cyber security policies, standards and guidelines.
  • Ensure alignment with relevant cyber security regulations, legislation and industry frameworks.
  • Communicate cyber security risks, priorities and technical debt to executive and business leadership teams.
  • Deliver cyber security awareness activities, workshops and mentoring sessions for technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Support compliance initiatives and drive improvements in security posture across IT and Operational Technology (OT) environments.
  • Develop reporting and metrics to measure cyber security maturity and effectiveness.
  • Act as a senior point of escalation and provide leadership support when required.
About You

To be successful in this role, you will bring strong cyber security advisory experience, excellent stakeholder engagement skills and the ability to translate complex technical concepts into practical business outcomes.

You will ideally have:
  • Demonstrated experience leading cyber security advisory and consulting engagements within Public Sector and/or Government environments.
  • Proven experience across Cyber Security, IT/OT Security, Technology Risk or Information Security.
  • Strong understanding of Australian cyber security legislation and regulatory requirements, including the Security of Critical Infrastructure (SoCI) Act and Privacy Act.
  • Experience working with recognised industry frameworks and standards such as:
    • NIST Cyber Security Framework (CSF)
    • ISA/IEC 62443
    • MITRE ATT&CK
    • D3FEND
    • Australian Energy Sector Cyber Security Framework (AESCSF)
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to influence stakeholders at all levels.
  • Strong programme and project delivery experience.
  • Proven ability to communicate complex cyber risks in clear business language.
  • Experience in risk management, governance and compliance environment.

If you're a seasoned Cyber Security professional looking to make an impact within a complex and critical environment, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply now to be considered.

At Chandler Macleod, we are committed to fostering a diverse workforce where everyone is welcome. We encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, women, neurodiverse, people living with a disability and the LGBTIQA+ community.

You can read more about our commitment to diversity and inclusion at https://www.chandlermacleod.com/diversity-and-inclusion.

job.title: Technical Sales Manager
job.description:
Kalgoorlie, WA | Residential Role | Company Vehicle | Relocation Support

Are you an experienced mining professional with a strong background in ESCO Ground Engaging Tools (GET), buckets, lips and wear components?

Have you worked in Kalgoorlie and developed strong site-level relationships across the Goldfields?

This is an outstanding opportunity to join a global leader in mining technology and wear solutions, taking ownership of key customer relationships and supporting some of Western Australia's most significant surface mining operations.

This is a residential Kalgoorlie position. FIFO applications will not be considered.

About the Opportunity
As the company's on-site ESCO representative, you will be responsible for supporting existing customers, monitoring product performance, identifying growth opportunities and defending market share across a portfolio of large mining operations throughout the Goldfields region.

You will become the trusted technical advisor for customers, providing expert guidance on ESCO wear products, conducting inspections, delivering performance reports and identifying opportunities to improve productivity and reduce operating costs.

Success in this role will come from your ability to build strong site relationships, understand mining operations, and leverage your existing Goldfields network to influence decisions and drive commercial outcomes.

What We're Looking For To be successful, you will ideally bring:
  • Previous hands-on experience with ESCO products, GET systems, buckets, lips and wear components
  • Strong understanding of surface mining operations and heavy mobile equipment
  • Existing relationships and networks across Kalgoorlie and Goldfields mine sites
  • Demonstrated experience conducting bucket inspections, wear analysis and product performance reporting
  • Ability to identify opportunities for product conversions and market share growth
  • Strong customer engagement and stakeholder management skills
  • Experience working directly with maintenance, reliability, planning and operational teams
  • Salesforce CRM experience highly regarded
  • Current driver's licence
Essential Requirements
  • Minimum 5 years' experience within the mining industry
  • Previous experience in a technical, product support, field service or mining sales support role
  • Existing knowledge of ESCO products and applications
  • Prior work history in the Kalgoorlie region with established site contacts and industry networks
  • Ability to travel regularly across customer operations throughout the Goldfields
What's On Offer
  • Highly competitive salary package
  • Fully maintained company vehicle
  • Four weeks' temporary accommodation assistance
  • Long-term career opportunity with a global industry leader
  • Autonomy to manage key accounts and customer relationships
  • Exposure to major mining operations and decision-makers
  • Opportunity to influence product performance, market growth and customer outcomes
Why Apply?

This role is not suited to someone looking to learn ESCO products from scratch.

We are seeking a proven mining industry professional who already understands ESCO applications, has credibility on mine sites, and can leverage established relationships across the Kalgoorlie region to immediately add value.

If you have the technical expertise, commercial mindset and Goldfields network to become a trusted advisor to mining customers, we would welcome your application.

job.title: Principal Coordinator - Roads & Civil Infrastructure
job.description:
Permanent | Senior Leadership | Civil Construction & Road Maintenance

For an experienced civil construction leader, this is an opportunity to step beyond individual projects and take ownership of an entire works program.

We are partnering with a regional Queensland local government organisation seeking an accomplished infrastructure professional to lead the planning and delivery of its road construction, maintenance and grading programs.

This isn't a role sitting several layers removed from delivery. You'll be working across both the strategic and operational sides of infrastructure, leading multidisciplinary teams and providing direction across complex works programs while ensuring projects are delivered safely, efficiently and to the required standard.

You'll have the opportunity to influence how programs are planned, prioritised and delivered, improve operational performance and provide trusted technical advice to senior stakeholders.

What you'll be responsible for:
Your remit will span a substantial portfolio of civil construction and maintenance activities, including:
  • Leading road construction, maintenance, grading and associated civil works programs
  • Managing supervisors, operational teams, contractors and multidisciplinary resources
  • Developing works programs, estimates, schedules and delivery priorities
  • Driving improvements across safety, productivity, cost, quality and delivery performance
  • Managing competing operational priorities across a geographically dispersed network
  • Providing senior technical and operational advice on infrastructure delivery

Who we're looking for We're deliberately looking for someone who has spent considerable time leading civil works in the field and at program level, rather than someone whose experience has been primarily design or consultancy based.
To be seriously considered, you'll need to bring:
  • A minimum of 15 years' experience in civil construction and road maintenance/grading operations
  • Demonstrated leadership of multidisciplinary civil construction or maintenance teams
  • Strong experience developing and delivering complex road works programs, including planning, estimating, scheduling and contractor management
  • A track record of delivering works safely and successfully across cost, quality and program requirements
  • The judgement and communication skills to operate as a senior technical and operational leader
A Civil Engineering qualification and/or formal Project Management qualifications will be highly regarded.

You'll also need to hold a Queensland C Class Manual Driver Licence and current General Safety Induction Card.


Why consider a regional move? For someone open to establishing themselves in regional Queensland, the overall employment package is designed to make the move genuinely attractive:
  • Permanent senior leadership position
  • Private-use vehicle
  • Up to $10,000 relocation assistance (Role is based in Biloela)
  • Subsidised housing assistance
  • Five weeks' annual leave
  • Professional membership fees covered
  • Ongoing professional development and training

This could particularly suit an experienced Works Manager, Construction Manager, Civil Operations Manager, Infrastructure Manager, Senior Project Manager or senior Council/TMR professional who has built their career around road construction and maintenance and is ready for broader ownership of a regional infrastructure program.


If your experience aligns and you'd like a confidential discussion about the organisation, location, package and scope of the position, apply now or contact Anna Dziopa at Chandler Macleod - 07 2140 6649.
job.salary: Up to $140K + super + private-use vehicle + relocation

job.title: Project Costing Services Officer
job.description:
Chandler Macleod is recruiting on behalf of our client for an experienced Project Costing Officer to support a large-scale Defence capability and investment environment. This opportunity is ideal for a finance, commercial, costing or project professional with experience developing cost models, affordability assessments and investment analysis within complex program environments.

Working with a broad range of stakeholders, you will play a key role in developing and maintaining cost estimates, supporting investment planning activities, and providing financial analysis that informs strategic decision-making and future capability outcomes.

About the Role
As a Project Costing Officer, you will provide specialist costing and financial analysis services to support the planning, prioritisation and delivery of complex capability initiatives.
You will work closely with program teams, finance stakeholders and senior decision-makers to ensure cost information is robust, traceable and supports informed investment decisions. The role requires strong analytical capability, attention to detail and the ability to communicate complex financial information to diverse stakeholders.

Key Responsibilities
  • Develop, maintain and update cost estimates and financial models
  • Coordinate costing activities across multiple projects and work streams
  • Conduct affordability assessments and investment option analysis
  • Prepare cost forecasts, expenditure analysis and budget planning information
  • Maintain supporting evidence, assumptions and cost traceability documentation
  • Prepare financial reports, governance papers, briefings and decision-support materials
  • Analyse financial impacts of competing investment priorities
  • Engage with finance, project and program stakeholders to support planning activities
  • Contribute to governance, audit and assurance requirements
  • Provide costing expertise across broader program initiatives as required

Required Skills & Experience
  • Strong experience in cost modelling, financial analysis or project costing
  • Advanced analytical and problem-solving capabilities
  • Ability to develop, maintain and explain complex cost models
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Excellent Microsoft Office skills, particularly Excel
  • Ability to present financial and commercial information clearly to stakeholders

Highly Regarded
  • Experience in Defence, Government or large complex program environments
  • Background in financial management, budgeting or cost estimation
  • Experience supporting business cases, investment decisions or governance processes
  • Knowledge of project, program or portfolio management practices
  • Qualifications in Finance, Commerce, Economics, Business, Engineering or a related discipline
  • Experience undertaking affordability, investment or schedule analysis

Requirements
  • Current NV1 Security Clearance is mandatory
  • Ability to work on-site in Canberra
  • Ability to prepare a concise resume and selection criteria response

Why Apply? This is an excellent opportunity to contribute to strategic capability planning and investment activities within a highly complex and rewarding environment. You will work alongside experienced professionals while providing critical costing and financial analysis that supports major organisational outcomes.

job.title: QHSE Manager
job.description:
About the Company

Since 1973, our client has been designing and manufacturing innovative electric heating solutions that keep industries running safely and efficiently. With more than 50 years of expertise, 750 employees, and 10 manufacturing plants, they support 30,000 customers across 100 countries.

Their mission is simple but powerful: to decarbonise industrial processes while creating value for customers, communities, and the planet.

The Opportunity

We are seeking a hands-on, proactive QHSE Manager to strengthen and elevate Quality, Health, Safety, and Environmental performance across the site.
This role is both strategic and operational—perfect for someone who enjoys rolling up their sleeves, working closely with teams, and driving continuous improvement. While you won’t have direct reports, you will collaborate across multiple departments and be supported by a strong national and global QHSE network within the Spirax Group.
The company welcomes applicants who may not have previously held the title “Manager” but who have proven responsibility for HSE within industrial, manufacturing, or operational settings. For the right person, this position offers genuine growth opportunities, including support for further training and higher-level qualifications.

About You

You will bring demonstrated experience in HSE or QHSE within a production, operational, or manufacturing environment. You understand quality systems, auditing, and risk management, and you have the confidence to engage with people at all levels.
You will also bring:
  • Minimum BSB41419 Certificate IV in Work Health & Safety (or equivalent)
  • Experience supporting or leading QHSE initiatives
  • Strong communication and stakeholder engagement skills
  • High attention to detail and the ability to manage competing priorities
  • A hands-on, collaborative approach that promotes safety and quality across the business
  • Additional qualifications in Quality Management Systems or advanced HSE (highly regarded)
Key Responsibilities

As the QHSE Manager, you will play a crucial role in ensuring a safe, compliant, and high‑performing workplace. Your responsibilities will include:
  • Developing and maintaining QHSE policies, procedures, and systems
  • Conducting risk assessments and implementing mitigation strategies
  • Investigating incidents and leading corrective and preventive actions
  • Delivering QHSE training and building a culture of safety and quality
  • Leading internal audits, inspections, and performance reporting
  • Overseeing environmental initiatives, including waste and pollution management
  • Promoting “Right First Time” quality practices across production and engineering
  • Managing emergency response planning and safety drills
  • Ensuring contractor and supplier compliance
  • Working cross‑functionally with operations, HR, maintenance, and engineering
  • Liaising with global QHSE teams across Europe, APAC, and the wider Spirax Group
  • Maintaining accurate records for audits, compliance, training, and incidents
  • Overseeing procurement related to safety and quality requirements
Why Join?
  • Be part of a respected global leader driving industrial sustainability and innovation
  • Enjoy a supportive environment with strong networks locally and internationally
  • Access genuine opportunities for learning, development, and career growth
  • Contribute to safety, quality, and environmental excellence
  • Competitive salary and long-term career potential
Ready to Make a Difference?

Apply now and take the lead in shaping a safe, high-quality, and sustainable future. For a confidential discussion, please contact Jo Ellerman on (02) 6691 9106.

job.title: Senior Clinician - Social Worker
job.description:
About the company:

Our client is a large federal government agency focused on providing high quality mental health assessment and clinical counselling services. They take pride on meeting client needs through a combination of proven clinical practices and new and emerging evidence-based approaches. Reporting to the Assistant Director, you will work with a professional team who are all dedicated to making a different in the lives of their clients.


About the role:

The successful candidate will deliver critical mental health support to clients, assess their needs, develop tailored intervention plans, and contribute to a team focused on improving outcomes for veterans. Your role will involve collaborating with multidisciplinary teams, maintaining detailed documentation, and ensuring compliance with departmental standards. This position offers a rewarding chance to impact lives positively while expanding your professional experience in a supportive, mission-driven setting.
 

  • Support regional teams by reviewing and allocating clients for counselling services, ensuring they are suitable for both initial and ongoing support in line with service guidelines.
  • Make sure all work follows clinical policies and that the correct forms and templates are used (such as intake, risk assessment, and care planning documents).
  • Provide quality counselling and support services — including risk assessment, referrals, individual, couple, and family sessions, and case management — to help clients achieve their goals.
  • Keep accurate and confidential client records, including session notes, care plans, risk assessments, and other updates in the client management system.
  • Take part in professional development and clinical supervision to maintain your professional registration.
  • Follow all relevant laws, ethical standards, and policies related to client care.
  • Meet regularly with your manager and other clinicians to discuss client progress and care plans.
  • Work with clients’ families and other treatment providers to make sure care is well-coordinated.
  • Contribute to a safe, supportive, and professional work environment that aligns with organisational values and goals.


About you:
  • You will have current registration with the Australian Health Practitioners Registration Agency (AHPRA) or Australian Association of Social Workers (AASW)
  • You will have Working with Children (WWC) and/or Vulnerable People Checks/Clearance (Blue Card) ideally, or have it granted before commencing the role
  • You will have experience in a similar clinical role
  • You will have extensive case management experience
  • You will be passionate about clinical psychology and social work to support mental health initiatives
  • You will have excellent interpersonal skills with competence in the provision of trauma informed, holistic, client centered intake, assessment and brief intervention with vulnerable clients
  • You will have experience providing support and intervention over the telephone for clients presenting a high risk of suicidality and apply appropriate assessment and safety planning
  • You will have ability to complete clinically appropriate intake assessment and documentation with formulated risk assessments which are tailored, appropriate, and actioned in accordance with presenting risk
  • Clinicians work in a rostered environment across between 7 am and 7pm on business days within a hybrid work from office/home model providing over the phone clinical services for Australian veterans and their families.


Benefits:
  • Casual temp contract to start ASAP (pending federal police clearance)
  • Long term temporary contract for 12 months
  • $67.24 per hour plus super
  • Full-time role Monday to Friday
  • Newcastle Location

job.title: Project and Program Cost Analyst

job.title: Senior Clinician - Mental Health Nurse
job.description:
About the company:

Our client is a large federal government agency focused on providing high quality mental health assessment and clinical counselling services. They take pride on meeting client needs through a combination of proven clinical practices and new and emerging evidence-based approaches. Reporting to the Assistant Director, you will work with a professional team who are all dedicated to making a different in the lives of their clients.


About the role:

The successful candidate will deliver critical mental health support to clients, assess their needs, develop tailored intervention plans, and contribute to a team focused on improving outcomes for veterans. Your role will involve collaborating with multidisciplinary teams, maintaining detailed documentation, and ensuring compliance with departmental standards. This position offers a rewarding chance to impact lives positively while expanding your professional experience in a supportive, mission-driven setting.
 

  • Support regional teams by reviewing and allocating clients for counselling services, ensuring they are suitable for both initial and ongoing support in line with service guidelines.
  • Make sure all work follows clinical policies and that the correct forms and templates are used (such as intake, risk assessment, and care planning documents).
  • Provide quality counselling and support services — including risk assessment, referrals, individual, couple, and family sessions, and case management — to help clients achieve their goals.
  • Keep accurate and confidential client records, including session notes, care plans, risk assessments, and other updates in the client management system.
  • Take part in professional development and clinical supervision to maintain your professional registration.
  • Follow all relevant laws, ethical standards, and policies related to client care.
  • Meet regularly with your manager and other clinicians to discuss client progress and care plans.
  • Work with clients’ families and other treatment providers to make sure care is well-coordinated.
  • Contribute to a safe, supportive, and professional work environment that aligns with organisational values and goals.


About you:
  • You will have current registration with the Australian Health Practitioners Registration Agency (AHPRA) or Australian Association of Social Workers (AASW)
  • You will have Working with Children (WWC) and/or Vulnerable People Checks/Clearance (Blue Card) ideally, or have it granted before commencing the role
  • You will have experience in a similar clinical role
  • You will have extensive case management experience
  • You will be passionate about clinical psychology and social work to support mental health initiatives
  • You will have excellent interpersonal skills with competence in the provision of trauma informed, holistic, client centered intake, assessment and brief intervention with vulnerable clients
  • You will have experience providing support and intervention over the telephone for clients presenting a high risk of suicidality and apply appropriate assessment and safety planning
  • You will have ability to complete clinically appropriate intake assessment and documentation with formulated risk assessments which are tailored, appropriate, and actioned in accordance with presenting risk
  • Clinicians work in a rostered environment across between 7 am and 7pm on business days within a hybrid work from office/home model providing over the phone clinical services for Australian veterans and their families.

About the Opportunity

Rio Tinto is a global mining and materials company operating in 35 countries, producing the materials essential to modern life. Their operations are built on safety, innovation, inclusion and creating value for communities, customers and shareholders.

Through Rio Tinto’s partnership with Chandler Macleod, we are seeking an experienced Project Engineer with Marine experience.

This is a newly created Project Engineer position supporting a major structural integrity program on the PPT Wharf in Dampier. Working on an 8:6 roster, you will oversee contractors, coordinate structural remediation works, manage quality and project documentation, and help deliver critical shutdown activities within a live operational marine environment. The role requires a self-motivated and adaptable professional who can navigate changing priorities, solve problems on the ground, and contribute to the successful delivery of this project.
 
Reporting to the Superintendent Delivery and working in a collaborative and exciting environment, you will:
  • Manage the day-to-day delivery of structural integrity works on a major wharf infrastructure project, ensuring scope, schedule and safety requirements are achieved.
  • Oversee contractor activities on site, providing direction, support and resolution of technical and operational issues as they arise.
  • Coordinate and monitor structural remediation works including blast and paint programs, structural steel repairs and replacement of beams and other infrastructure components.
  • Review, assess and respond to contractor technical queries, making practical engineering decisions in a fast-paced operational environment.
  • Conduct on-site verification of completed works, including quality inspections, quantity measurements and management of project documentation.
  • Support shutdown and outage execution activities, including schedule validation, stakeholder coordination and attendance at shutdown planning meetings.
  • Manage quality outcomes and defect close-out processes, ensuring compliance with project specifications and documentation requirements.
  • Adapt to changing project priorities, identifying alternative work scopes and maintaining project momentum when operational constraints or schedule changes impact planned activities.

About You
  • Proven structural integrity project experience in industrial or marine environments.
  • Proactive problem-solver with strong decision-making and adaptability.
  • Structural engineering qualification or relevant trade background with site delivery experience.
  • Resilient, hands-on professional who thrives in challenging operational environments.
  • Strong teamwork and communication skills
  • Dedication to everyone’s safety
  • Current C Class manual drivers’ license
  • Relevant trade qualifications and certificates
  • Ability to pass pre-employment medical and other testing

Chandler Macleod is one of Australia’s most experienced workforce partners. You’ll receive a competitive pay rate paid weekly, superannuation on all hours worked, access to our Employee Assistance Program, a dedicated Chandler-Rio Tinto support team, simple digital onboarding, and access to future Rio Tinto assignments.

job.title: Steel Fixers
job.description:
About the role
Great opportunity for experienced Steel Fixers to join a busy precast yard in Woolgoolga, NSW. You’ll be working hands-on with reinforcement steel for precast moulds—reading drawings, preparing and tying rebar, and ensuring reinforcement is set correctly prior to concrete pours.

 
Duties
  • Read reinforcing steel drawings and specifications
  • Measure, cut and bend reinforcing bar (rebar) to required sizes
  • Assemble and fix reinforcement cages and steel frames
  • Tie reinforcement using tie wire and hand tools
  • Position reinforcement, mesh, starter bars, ligatures and components inside precast moulds
  • Install spacers and maintain required concrete cover
  • Check dimensions, spacing and positioning against drawings
  • Operate tools/equipment (rebar cutters, benders, grinders, tying tools)
  • Assist with setting up and stripping precast moulds as required
  • Move/position reinforcing steel and materials around the yard
  • Maintain a clean, safe work area and follow WHS procedures/PPE requirements
  • Work closely with concrete crews, formworkers, and crane/production teams to prepare moulds for pouring
 
Skills and Experience
  • Proven steel fixing experience (ideally within precast or similar production environments)
  • Ability to read and work from reo/reinforcement drawings and specs
  • Confident cutting, bending, tying, and placing reo to measurement/tolerance requirements
  • Strong safety mindset and ability to work efficiently in a team environment
 
Desirable:
  • Experience working in precast yards / mould preparation environments
  • Ability to operate common yard tools and equipment safely (cutters/benders/grinders)
 
Benefits
  • Competitive hourly rate ($45–$50/hr + super, depending on skills & experience)
  • Full-time hours (40 hours/week)
  • Local Woolgoolga role with an established precast operation
 
How to apply

job.title: Recruitment Consultant
job.description:
Recruitment Consultant (3-Month temporary assignment)

Are you an experienced recruiter who thrives in a fast-paced environment and enjoys the challenge of finding great talent? We're looking for a Recruitment Consultant to join our Newcastle team to support a period of increased recruitment activity.

This is a fantastic opportunity to work alongside an experienced and energetic team, build your recruitment expertise and contribute to delivering exceptional outcomes for our clients.

  • Be part of a fun, supportive and collaborative team

  • Make an immediate impact during a peak volume recruitment period

  • Initial 3-month assignment with potential to extend into 2027

About Chandler Macleod
Chandler Macleod is one of Australasia's leading providers of integrated people services. We partner with organisations across a broad range of industries to help them attract, engage and retain great talent.

Our success is built on a culture that empowers our people to be authentic, collaborative and client-focused. We value ownership, respect, innovation and doing the right thing, and we're passionate about creating opportunities that help people and organisations reach their potential.

About the Role
Working closely with our experienced consultants, you will provide recruitment support across a diverse portfolio of clients and roles. This is a hands-on position where you'll contribute to the delivery of quality recruitment outcomes while developing strong candidate and client relationships.
  • Assist with sourcing candidates through job boards, databases, and proactive search methods

  • Candidate screening, interviewing and shortlisting

  • Build and maintain talent pipelines for current and future hiring needs

  • ork closely with consultants to manage workload and ensure efficient delivery of roles

  • Maintain and utilise recruitment systems ensuring data integrity and system compliance

About You
We're looking for someone who brings positive energy, initiative and a team-first attitude.

You enjoy working in a fast-moving environment, can manage competing priorities and are comfortable engaging with candidates across a variety of industries and skill levels.

Ideally, you will:
  • Have approx. 1-2 years experience executing recruitment across industrial, engineering, manufacturing, technical or high-volume environments.

  • Apply a mature and flexible approach to providing adhoc support as needed

  • Actively engage and collaborate with your teammates to foster a fun and positive culture.

  • Have a detailed understanding of best practice recruitment methodology, systems and processes.

  • Most importantly, you'll be someone who enjoys being part of a team, contributes positively to the workplace culture and is happy to roll up their sleeves to help wherever needed.

Ready to Apply?

job.description:

About the company:

This Federal Government agency works to deliver programs and services that support people with disability and their families, aiming to improve access, engagement, and outcomes across Australia. The agency collaborates closely with communities, service providers, and government stakeholders to implement initiatives that enhance social inclusion, wellbeing, and equity.


About the role:

  • Providing counter/reception support for the local office including participant enquiries in the self-help kiosks and the Agency online support.

job.title: Local Community Connector
job.description:
Chandler Macleod is recruiting on behalf of our client for multiple APS4 Local Community Connector opportunities across Western Australia. This is an exciting 12-month assignment supporting people with disability, their families, carers, and communities to access information, services, and supports.

Working within a community-focused environment, you will play a key role in building relationships, promoting inclusion, and supporting individuals to connect with the National Disability Insurance Scheme (NDIS) and broader community services.

Available Locations
  • Albany, WA
  • Northam, WA
  • Carnarvon, WA
  • Kalgoorlie, WA

What's on Offer
  • 12-month contract opportunity
  • $43.82 per hour + super
  • Meaningful work supporting local communities
  • Opportunity to engage directly with participants and stakeholders
  • Travel and community engagement across regional and remote areas

About the Role As a Local Community Connector, you will provide a visible, local presence within the community and support people to navigate available services and pathways. You will work collaboratively with participants, service providers, community groups, and internal stakeholders to promote participation, inclusion, and positive outcomes.

Key Responsibilities
  • Provide information about disability supports, community services, and available programs
  • Support participants and service providers by gathering and verifying information
  • Assist with participant plan implementation, monitoring, and ongoing engagement
  • Develop and maintain strong relationships with local community stakeholders
  • Promote inclusive and culturally safe community participation
  • Conduct participant check-ins and support evidence gathering activities
  • Complete administrative tasks and maintain accurate records
  • Participate in outreach activities within regional and remote communities

About You To be successful, you will demonstrate:

Customer Service & Community Engagement
  • Experience delivering high-quality customer service within community, government, health, or service-focused environments
  • Ability to respond to enquiries, resolve issues, and provide accurate information
  • Strong communication and stakeholder engagement skills

ICT Capability
  • Experience using databases, case management systems, and Microsoft Office applications
  • Ability to maintain accurate records and support reporting activities
  • Confidence working across multiple digital systems

First Nations Cultural Capability
  • Understanding of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander cultures, histories, and communities
  • Demonstrated ability to engage respectfully and effectively with First Nations peoples
  • Experience contributing to culturally safe and inclusive environments

Role Requirements
  • Ability to travel within regional and remote communities, including overnight stays
  • Current driver's licence and willingness to drive long distances when required
  • Comfortable undertaking community outreach, face-to-face engagement, and phone-based support
  • Ability to work in office, community, and occasional work-from-home environments
  • Capacity to navigate varied locations and terrains as part of community engagement activities

Why Apply? This is a rewarding opportunity to make a genuine difference in local communities while working with a dedicated team focused on improving outcomes for people with disability. If you are passionate about community engagement, inclusion, and delivering exceptional service, we encourage you to apply.

job.title: Project Officers
job.description:
Chandler Macleod is recruiting on behalf of our client for an experienced Project Officer  to support the delivery of critical projects and programs within a highly secure Federal Government environment.
 

Working within a Project, Program or Portfolio Management Office (PMO), you will play a key role in supporting project planning, governance, reporting, financial management and delivery activities. This opportunity is suited to a motivated project professional who enjoys working in structured environments and contributing to complex, high-priority initiatives.

About the Role In this position, you will:

  • Support the delivery of projects and programs through effective project coordination and administrative support.
  • Assist with project planning, scheduling, monitoring and reporting activities.
  • Support project testing, evaluation and acceptance activities.
  • Apply established project management methodologies, tools and processes across administrative and technical project activities.
  • Research, prepare and coordinate briefs, reports, submissions and correspondence.
  • Assist with committee papers, governance documentation and project reporting requirements.
  • Maintain project records, schedules, registers and delivery documentation.
  • Support project governance activities, meetings and stakeholder engagement.
  • Assist with project risk, issue and change management processes.
  • Maintain project financial records and support budget monitoring activities.
  • Contribute to quality assurance and project control activities across the program environment.
Key Criteria to be Successful To be successful in this role, you will demonstrate:

  • Experience supporting projects, programs or PMO functions within a structured delivery environment.
  • Knowledge of project management methodologies, frameworks and tools.
  • Experience coordinating project planning, scheduling, tracking and reporting activities.
  • Strong organisational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines.
  • Experience preparing project documentation, reports, briefings and governance artefacts.
  • Strong attention to detail and ability to maintain accurate project records and documentation.
  • Experience supporting project governance forums, project control boards or assurance activities.
  • Ability to analyse information and provide practical recommendations to support project delivery.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement and communication skills.
  • Ability to work independently while contributing effectively within a collaborative project team environment.
Desirable Experience
  • Experience supporting portfolio, program or project management office activities.
  • Exposure to project financial management, risk management and quality assurance processes.
  • Experience using project management and scheduling tools.
  • Previous experience within Federal Government, Defence or National Security environments.
  • Knowledge of project lifecycle management and governance frameworks.
Security Requirements
  • Current TSPV Security Clearance is mandatory at the time of submission.
  • Successful candidates will be required to complete an Organisation Suitability Assessment (OSA) prior to commencement.
Role Details
  • Position: Project Officer
  • Location: Canberra, ACT
  • Working Arrangement: Onsite (subject to operational requirements)
  • Hours: 40 hours per week
  • Start Date: 30 November 2026
  • Contract: 12-month initial engagement with 2 x 12-month extension options available
About the Opportunity This role offers the opportunity to contribute to nationally significant projects supporting critical government capabilities. You will work alongside experienced project professionals, gain exposure to complex delivery environments and play an important role in supporting project outcomes from planning through to execution.

If you have strong project coordination experience, excellent organisational skills and a background supporting project delivery in complex environments, we encourage you to apply.

job.title: Assistant Director, Facilities and Security
job.description:
Chandler Macleod is recruiting on behalf of our client for an experienced Assistant Director, Facilities and Security to lead and coordinate critical property, facilities, security and business continuity activities within a Federal Government environment.

This role will play a key leadership function, ensuring facilities and security operations meet compliance obligations while driving continuous improvement across governance, assurance, workplace management and risk management frameworks. Working closely with internal stakeholders, service providers and senior leadership, you will deliver practical solutions that support operational excellence and organisational resilience.

This opportunity is ideal for a proactive property and security professional who enjoys balancing strategic advisory responsibilities with hands-on operational delivery.

About the Role In this position, you will:

  • Lead the identification, management and resolution of office accommodation defects, maintenance requirements and facilities-related issues.
  • Coordinate facilities and property services through landlords, property managers, contractors and whole-of-government service providers.
  • Assess physical, personnel and travel security arrangements and implement risk mitigation strategies.
  • Support compliance with the Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF), including reporting, assurance activities and continuous improvement initiatives.
  • Coordinate whole-of-government property reporting, planning and sustainability obligations.
  • Lead a post-occupancy review of office accommodation and provide recommendations to improve workspace functionality and utilisation.
  • Improve visitor management, access controls, security incident processes and risk management arrangements.
  • Develop and implement policies, procedures, frameworks and assurance mechanisms relating to facilities management, security and business continuity.

job.title: General Manager
job.description:
General Manager - West Coast Operations
Perth, WA

An outstanding opportunity exists for an accomplished General Manager to lead the Western Australian operations of a highly regarded Australian manufacturing business with a long-standing reputation for quality, innovation and customer excellence.
With a strong market position, established national footprint and ambitious growth agenda, the business designs, manufactures and delivers premium solutions across residential, commercial and industrial markets. Built on a foundation of performance, reliability and continuous improvement, the organisation is now seeking a commercially astute leader to drive the next phase of growth and operational excellence across Western Australia.

Reporting to the Managing Director and working closely with the Executive Leadership Team, you will have full accountability for the performance of the West Coast business, leading manufacturing, distribution, customer service, sales and field operations while delivering strong financial, operational and cultural outcomes.

The Opportunity
This is a genuine leadership role offering end-to-end responsibility for a significant business unit. You will be responsible for developing and executing the WA business strategy, driving operational performance, strengthening customer relationships and building a high-performing culture focused on accountability, safety and continuous improvement.
You will play a critical role in identifying growth opportunities, optimising operational efficiency and ensuring the business continues to deliver exceptional outcomes for customers and stakeholders.

Key Responsibilities
Strategic Leadership & Commercial Performance
  • Develop and execute the West Coast business strategy aligned with national objectives.
  • Deliver sustainable revenue growth, profitability and market expansion.
  • Identify and pursue new market opportunities and strategic initiatives.
  • Lead financial planning, budgeting, forecasting and performance reporting.
  • Drive commercial decision-making through strong financial and operational analysis.
Operational Excellence
  • Lead end-to-end operations across manufacturing, warehousing, logistics and customer delivery.
  • Improve productivity, efficiency, quality and service performance.
  • Embed continuous improvement initiatives that reduce waste, improve throughput and enhance customer outcomes.
  • Ensure facilities, assets and equipment are maintained to support operational reliability.
  • Drive performance against key operational metrics including quality, delivery and cost.
People Leadership
  • Build, mentor and develop an engaged, high-performing leadership team.
  • Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration and continuous improvement.
  • Lead workforce planning, capability development and talent management initiatives.
  • Champion workplace safety and wellbeing across all operations.
  • Create an environment that attracts, develops and retains top talent.
Customer & Stakeholder Engagement
  • Build strong relationships with key customers, suppliers and strategic partners.
  • Support business development initiatives across builder, reseller and industrial channels.
  • Ensure exceptional service delivery and customer satisfaction.
  • Represent the organisation across the WA market and broader industry networks.
About You
To be successful in this role you will bring:
  • Proven experience as a General Manager, State Manager, Operations Manager or equivalent senior leadership position.
  • A strong background within manufacturing, distribution, building products, construction, industrial services or a related sector.
  • Demonstrated success leading diverse operational teams and delivering commercial results.
  • Strong financial acumen with experience managing budgets, P&L performance and strategic planning.
  • A track record of driving operational improvement and organisational growth.
  • Exceptional leadership, communication and stakeholder management skills.
  • A genuine commitment to safety, quality and continuous improvement.
Tertiary qualifications in Business, Engineering, Operations Management or a related discipline will be highly regarded.

What's on Offer
  • Executive-level leadership opportunity with significant influence and autonomy.
  • Well-established Australian business with a strong reputation and growth trajectory.
  • Broad operational and commercial responsibility.
  • Opportunity to shape strategy and drive meaningful business outcomes.
  • Competitive executive remuneration package.
Applicants must have unrestricted Australian working rights and be based in, or willing to relocate to, Perth, Western Australia.

If you are a commercially minded leader with a proven track record of delivering growth, operational excellence and high-performing teams, we welcome your application.

job.description:
Employment Type: Full-Time, Casual 
Length of Assignment: Two weeks with potential extension
Working Arrangement: 100% on-site, Bayswater
Hourly Rate: $58.75-$67.5 per hour + Super

About the Role
Our client is seeking an experienced Technical Estimator professional to join the team on an initial two-week contract, with the possibility of extension.

This role will suit someone with a strong background in timber, steel or manufacturing environments, combined with proven experience in estimating and quotations within the timber, steel or related building products sectors.

The successful candidate will be confident interpreting architectural plans, taking measurements, preparing quotations and communicating professionally with builders, joinery companies and other industry stakeholders.

You will play an important role in understanding project requirements, interpreting floor plans and determining the appropriate door and joinery requirements before preparing accurate quotations.
 
Key Responsibilities
  • Review and interpret architectural drawings and floor plans to identify door and joinery requirements.
  • Take and interpret measurements to determine appropriate door sizes, specifications and quantities.

  • Liaise with builders, contractors, suppliers and customers to project requirements.
  • Provide professional and confident communication over the phone and via email.
  • Use CAD and related design/technical software to interpret and support project requirements.
  • Work with 3CX phone systems and associated communication platforms.
  • Understand manufacturing processes and how design and specifications translate into production.
  • Work with and understand CNC manufacturing processes, including 5-axis CNC machinery.
  • Assist with general technical and estimating requirements across timber, steel and door manufacturing.
  • Ensure quotations and measurements are accurate and aligned with project specifications.
 
 
Skills and Experience
  • Previous experience within timber manufacturing, joinery, doors or a related manufacturing environment.
  • Previous experience in estimating and quoting
  • Strong ability to read and interpret architectural drawings and floor plans.
  • Confidence taking measurements and determining appropriate product requirements.
  • Experience working with CAD or CAD-related software.
  • Knowledge and experience with CNC machinery, particularly 5-axis machines.
  • Strong computer literacy.
  • Excellent phone manner and confident verbal communication skills.
  • Strong attention to detail and accuracy when preparing quotes.
  • The ability to make practical decisions based on drawings, measurements and project requirements.
  • A proactive approach and the ability to work independently

job.title: Change and Implementation Officer
job.description:
Chandler Macleod is recruiting on behalf of our client for an experienced Change and Implementation Officer to support the successful delivery of a significant organisational transformation program.

This role will lead change management, communications, training, business readiness and implementation activities across multiple workstreams. Working closely with senior leaders, project teams and business stakeholders, you will help prepare the organisation for change, drive adoption of new processes and systems, and ensure sustainable business outcomes.

This opportunity is ideal for a change professional who thrives in complex environments, enjoys engaging stakeholders at all levels and has a strong track record delivering successful change and implementation initiatives.

About the Role In this position, you will:

  • Develop and deliver integrated change and implementation plans across multiple workstreams.
  • Assess the impact of process and system changes on employees, teams and ways of working.
  • Lead stakeholder engagement, consultation and communication activities.
  • Design and coordinate training programs, support materials and user guidance.
  • Conduct business readiness assessments and identify adoption risks.
  • Support implementation activities and provide early-life operational support.
  • Monitor adoption, stakeholder feedback and business outcomes following implementation.
  • Develop procedures, templates and support documentation to enable long-term business ownership.
  • Work closely with project teams and senior stakeholders to deliver successful organisational change outcomes.
Key Criteria to be Successful To be successful in this role, you will demonstrate:

  • Extensive experience delivering change management, implementation or business adoption initiatives within complex organisations.
  • Proven ability to assess organisational impacts and support stakeholders through change.
  • Experience developing and delivering communication, consultation, engagement and training strategies.
  • Strong capability in business readiness assessment, risk identification and implementation planning.
  • Excellent stakeholder management skills with the ability to influence and build trusted relationships at all levels.
  • Highly developed written and verbal communication skills, including preparing communications, briefing materials and training content.
  • Strong planning, organisation and problem-solving skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and workstreams.
  • Relevant qualifications or significant equivalent experience in change management, organisational development, communications, learning or a related discipline.
Desirable Experience
  • Experience supporting enterprise-wide process, policy, finance or technology transformation programs.
  • Familiarity with structured change methodologies such as Prosci ADKAR, Kotter or similar frameworks.
  • Experience working within government, public sector or purpose-driven organisations.
  • Exposure to complex business transformation, systems implementation or operational improvement programs.
If you are an experienced change professional with a passion for stakeholder engagement, organisational transformation and delivering lasting business improvements, we encourage you to apply.

We're looking for someone who can bring strong practical production experience, attention to detail and the ability to lead people well. Depending on your experience and capability, the role could be suited to someone ready to step into a Production Supervisor position or an experienced Production Manager looking for a hands-on regional opportunity.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Assisting with quoting and estimating
  • Reading and interpreting engineering and fabrication drawings

What we're looking forIdeally, you'll have:

  • Experience reading and interpreting technical and engineering drawings
  • Experience managing people and coordinating a busy workshop
  • A practical understanding of production planning, quality and procurement
  • Experience dealing with workplace safety, and resolving issues
  • Strong attention to detail
  • A strong commitment to workplace safety and compliance
  • Good communication skills and the confidence to deal directly with clients
  • A hands-on, practical approach and the ability to make decisions
Experience with heavy fabrication, cranes, earth-moving equipment, vacuum trucks or similar heavy equipment would be highly regarded.
More than just managing productionWe're a harmonious team, and that matters to us.
We want people to enjoy coming to work and to be proud of what they produce. The person in this role will play an important part in maintaining that culture while ensuring the workshop is organised, productive and operating safely.
We're looking for someone who can lead rather than simply supervise — someone who is comfortable getting involved, supporting the team, dealing with issues as they arise and helping people perform at their best.
The working weekThis is a permanent, full-time position with a standard 38-hour week.
Typical hours are 6.00am–4.30pm Monday to Thursday, with a shorter six-hour day on Friday.
The Production Supervisor/Manager needs to be available for the hours the workshop is operating, with only occasional weekend work. Weekend requirements would typically be no more than a half day.

Role Description 

• Create supporting learning material such as audio, video, simulations, work instructions, quick reference guides, role plays, games etc. that align to client objectives.
• Build engaging exercises and course content that enhances the learning experience.
• Design assessment tools that appropriately measure learner competencies, including but not limited to knowledge and skills.

Key challenges
• Striking an effective and sustainable balance between a consistent Cluster wide approach to learning programs to support integration, collaboration and efficiency with requests for program tailoring to meet specific needs and secure business commitment.
• Maintaining a comprehensive knowledge of relevant legislation, regulations and industry requirements and reforms and their implications for training and development products and their delivery while keeping up to date with trends and best practice in learning technologies and instructional design.
• Ensuring that that learning, meets business needs, is aligned with best practice adult learning principles, complies with relevant legislation and regulations, and is consistently applied across the organisation while managing multiple deliverables to tight timelines in a changing environment.

Knowledge and experience
• Previous experience working within an instructional design team or group.
• Knowledge and understanding of the Standards for RTOs 2015.
• Demonstrated proficiency in the use of corporate computing systems and applications in creating documents, training artefacts materials, editing and publishing.

Essential requirements
• Proven experience in the development, implementation and evaluation of learning programs, products and artefacts.

job.title: Fitter
job.description:
Fitter

Chandler Macleod is seeking a trade-qualified Fitter to join an established industry leader specialising in truck-mounted cranes and mobile lifting solutions.

This is an excellent permanent opportunity for a practical, team-focused tradesperson looking to broaden their skills across mechanical fitting, hydraulics, fabrication, crane assembly and servicing.

While a Mechanical Fitter or Fitter and Turner is preferred, applications are also welcomed from Heavy Vehicle Mechanics, Plant Mechanics and Boilermakers with strong mechanical aptitude and a willingness to learn.

The Opportunity

Working within a close-knit workshop team, you will primarily assist with assembling new truck-mounted cranes, along with maintenance and service work.

Tradespeople generally work collaboratively in small teams, with everyone contributing across the broader manufacturing and assembly process. You won’t be restricted to one discipline—the team is looking for someone open-minded, adaptable and willing to assist wherever needed.

Your responsibilities may include:

  • Mechanical fitting and assembly of new truck-mounted cranes
  • Installing and working with hydraulic components and systems
  • Completing maintenance, servicing and mechanical repairs
  • Assisting with basic welding and fabrication work
  • Diagnosing mechanical and hydraulic faults
  • Working collaboratively with fitters, boilermakers and other trades
  • Maintaining a safe, organised and productive workshop

About You
You will ideally have:
  • A recognised trade qualification as a Mechanical Fitter, Fitter and Turner, Heavy Vehicle Mechanic, Plant Mechanic or Boilermaker
  • Strong mechanical aptitude and practical problem-solving skills
  • An interest in learning hydraulics, welding and other trade disciplines
  • A flexible attitude and willingness to contribute across all areas of the workshop
  • A team-focused approach and strong work ethic
  • A commitment to quality workmanship and safe work practices

What’s on Offer
  • Permanent, stable employment with OT available
  • Competitive rate of $43–$45 per hour, with some flexibility for an exceptional candidate
  • Specialist training in areas such as hydraulics and basic welding
  • Opportunities to become multi-skilled across crane assembly, fitting, fabrication, and servicing
  • Supportive team environment with exceptional employee tenure
  • Stable local, workshop-based work
  • Early finish every Friday
 

If you are an adaptable tradesperson looking for stable local work, excellent training, and the opportunity to expand your technical skills, we would love to hear from you.

Utility & Facilities Manager | Northmead, NSW
Lead facilities operations at a major industrial site while driving safety, compliance, and continuous improvement.

Our client is seeking an experienced Utility & Facilities Manager to oversee facilities management operations based in Northmead, NSW.

This is an exciting opportunity for a proactive, commercially minded facilities professional who thrives in complex operational environments and enjoys building strong stakeholder relationships while delivering high standards of service, compliance, and project execution.

About the Opportunity
Reporting to the Construction Manager, you will be responsible for managing facilities operations, contractor performance, compliance requirements, and facilities-related capital projects at a key production facility.

You will work closely with operational leaders, service providers, contractors, and internal stakeholders to ensure facilities are safe, compliant, efficient, and fit for purpose.

This role offers a blend of operational facilities management, contractor governance, budget oversight, and project delivery, making it an ideal opportunity for someone looking to make a tangible impact within a large-scale manufacturing environment.

Key Responsibilities
  • Manage the performance and relationship of external Facilities Management service providers.
  • Oversee delivery of both hard and soft facilities services, including planned and reactive maintenance, cleaning, landscaping, waste management, pest control, and statutory compliance.
  • Ensure facilities and building infrastructure are maintained safely, efficiently, and cost effectively.
  • Coordinate contractor activities and manage permit-to-work processes.
  • Monitor and drive compliance with health, safety, environmental, and regulatory requirements.
  • Lead facilities-related continuous improvement initiatives.
  • Provide regular reporting on facilities performance, budgets, risks, and project delivery.
  • Monitor operational expenditure and identify opportunities to improve value and cost efficiencies.
  • Manage minor capital works projects from planning and procurement through to completion and handover.
  • Partner with site leadership teams to support operational continuity and business objectives.
About You
To be successful in this role, you will bring:
  • Proven experience managing facilities management contracts, service providers, and contractors.
  • Experience delivering capital works projects within manufacturing, industrial, logistics, or commercial environments.
  • Strong knowledge of contractor management, permit-to-work systems, and workplace health and safety requirements.
  • Demonstrated budget management and cost-control experience.
  • Excellent stakeholder engagement and communication skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced operational environment.
  • Strong understanding of the National Construction Code (BCA) and relevant Australian Standards.
  • Qualifications in Facilities Management, Construction, Project Management, Engineering, or a related discipline.
  • Intermediate to advanced Microsoft Office skills.

  • Collaborative and supportive stakeholder environment.
  • Career growth within a well-established and highly regarded organisation.

job.title: Production Operator
job.description:
Production Operator
We are seeking reliable and motivated Production Operator to join our manufacturing client based in Beverley. This is a hands-on role working within a production environment, supporting the efficient operation of the product fill line and maintaining high-quality standards.
This position offers a Monday to Friday roster, with rotating day and afternoon shifts. Occasional weekend work may be required to meet production demands. You'll rotate through a variety of production tasks, providing plenty of variety throughout your workday while contributing to a safe and productive workplace.
 
Key Responsibilities
  • Rotate through various production and fill line tasks
  • Load buckets and lids onto the production line
  • Connect hoses and fill heads to support filling operations
  • Operate control panels and production equipment
  • Stack, wrap and prepare pallets for dispatch
  • Move raw materials and finished products throughout the site
  • Operate forklifts and other mobile plant equipment where licensed
  • Perform routine cleaning and housekeeping duties
  • Follow quality, safety and operational procedures at all times
About You
  • Previous experience in manufacturing, production, process work or machine operation is highly regarded
  • Comfortable working in a fast-paced environment
  • Physically fit and capable of manual handling tasks
  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to quality
  • Reliable, punctual and safety-focused
  • Able to work effectively as part of a team
  • Forklift licence is advantageous but not essential
Requirements
  • Full working rights within Australia
  • Availability to work rotating day and afternoon shifts between 6:00am and 8:45pm
  • Current driver's licence and reliable transport
  • Ability to pass a National Police Check
  • Ability to pass a pre-employment Drug and Alcohol Screen
What's on Offer?
  • Immediate start available
  • Competitive casual hourly rate of $46 per hour + penalties 
  • Full-time hours with rotating shifts
  • Variety of duties through regular task rotation
  • Supportive team environment
  • Potential for ongoing or permanent employment for suitable candidates
How to Apply
If you're looking for your next opportunity within the manufacturing industry and enjoy hands-on work in a team-focused environment, click APPLY NOW and submit your resume.
