job.title: Group Finance Manager
job.description:
Group Finance Manager, Multi-Entity Private Group
Campbelfield 

Our client is a privately owned, founder-led group of businesses with a combined annual turnover exceeding $30 million. The Group spans six operating entities across bin hire and property development, waste services, legal services, agriculture and wellness, all wholly owned by a single Director who moves fast and runs multiple projects at once.

This is not a conventional Group Finance Manager role. It's a genuine seat at the table with a founder who has built serious value across his businesses but knows his financial oversight hasn't kept pace with growth. Fund flows between entities haven't always been formally documented, and there's currently no single consolidated view of the Group's debt, cash or net asset position.

You'll be the first person to sit across the entire Group with a clear mandate: bring order, structure and visibility to the Director's complete financial position, business and personal.

Responsibilities
  • Owning the Group's consolidated financial position at all times, with the Director able to get an accurate answer to any financial question within the hour
  • Managing everything from personal expenses through to major capital requirements for property acquisitions and construction
  • Rolling cash flow forecasts and a weekly cash and debt summary for the Director
  • Overseeing the bookkeeping team and liaising with the external tax agent on compliance
  • Building and enforcing clear financial controls, including a formal intercompany transfer process
  • Supporting evaluation of new property acquisitions, including development feasibility modelling
  • Managing banking relationships and lender communication across a large number of accounts
What We're Looking For:
  • 7+ years in a senior finance role, ideally across multiple entities or a group structure
  • Comfortable working directly with a founder where priorities shift fast; you're a stabilising force, not an extra variable
  • Advanced Xero skills across multiple entities, without needing support
  • Experience managing or directing bookkeepers and junior finance staff
  • CPA or CA preferred, though exceptional experience will be considered in place of it
  • Absolute discretion; you'll have full visibility of the Director's personal and business financial position
Why This Role:

 At 30 days, you'll have delivered a complete financial map of the Group. At 6 months, clear controls are in place and the Director gets a weekly summary he can rely on. At 12 months, you're his most trusted operational partner, contributing directly to decisions on acquisitions, cash deployment and growth.

This is a genuinely broad, high-trust mandate for someone who wants ownership, not just oversight.

To apply, submit your CV along with a short cover note on why this particular role, its pace, complexity and scope, appeals to you.

job.title: Participant Support Officer
job.description:
Chandler Macleod is recruiting on behalf of our client for multiple Business Support Officer opportunities. This is a rewarding role where you'll play an important part in supporting participants through key stages of their journey, delivering quality customer service and helping to achieve positive outcomes.
Working within a collaborative and fast-paced environment, you will manage a variety of administrative, operational and customer-focused tasks while engaging with participants, providers and stakeholders across Australia. This a full time, office based, labour hire contract.

About the Role As a Participant Support Officer, you'll be responsible for managing a diverse workload, resolving enquiries, and supporting participants through established processes and pathways. You'll use a range of systems and tools to review information, assess participant matters, and ensure actions are completed accurately and within required timeframes.

This role requires strong judgement, empathy, attention to detail and the ability to communicate effectively with people from diverse backgrounds.

Key Responsibilities
  • Manage participant-related enquiries and provide accurate information and support.
  • Conduct reviews of participant information and maintain records across multiple systems.
  • Make outbound calls to participants, providers and stakeholders to gather information and progress matters.
  • Assess and action participant requests in line with legislation, policies and operational guidelines.
  • Escalate complex issues where required and contribute to achieving team service delivery outcomes.
  • Assist with process improvements, reporting activities and project-related initiatives.
  • Work collaboratively with team members to share knowledge, provide feedback and support continuous improvement.
About You To be successful in this role, you will demonstrate:
  • Exceptional communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to build rapport and engage with a broad range of stakeholders.
  • Strong customer service experience within a high-volume environment.
  • The ability to remain calm, professional and solution-focused when dealing with sensitive or complex situations.
  • Excellent organisational skills and the ability to manage competing priorities.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities.
  • A high level of attention to detail when working with data and documentation.
  • Experience interpreting policies, procedures or legislative frameworks.
  • Confidence using Microsoft Office and navigating multiple systems simultaneously.
What We're Looking For
  • Experience in administration, customer service, contact centres, case management, human services, health, government or community services environments.
  • Ability to handle sensitive information with professionalism and confidentiality.
  • Demonstrated resilience, adaptability and commitment to delivering positive customer outcomes.
  • A collaborative team player with a proactive approach to learning and continuous improvement.
For any queries, please contact volumefedgov@chandlermacleod.com

If you match the above criteria APPLY now

job.title: Catering Attendant EOI
job.description:
Chandler Macleod is seeking Expressions of Interest from reliable, hardworking Catering Attendants / Potwash to support our client’s industrial catering team based in Adelaide’s western suburbs.

These opportunities may suit people looking for ongoing and regular work in a clean, inclusive onsite environment, with onsite parking, full uniform, and meals provided.

Key responsibilities
  • Sorting and packing catering equipment
  • Fast-paced food preparation and meal plating
  • Repetitive manual handling and packing duties
  • General cleaning and hygiene tasks
  • Washing/cleaning equipment including cutlery and dishes
To be considered, you will ideally have
  • Recent, relevant experience in food manufacturing / high-volume food environments
  • Strong knowledge of food hygiene practices and quality standards
  • Good literacy and numeracy skills
  • Ability to pass a full medical and National Police Clearance
  • Flexibility to work day and afternoon shifts across a 7-day roster
  • Reliable car and licence
  • Full working rights and strong availability
  • Proven reliability, initiative, and strong work ethic
Important: This role does not count towards the 88 days requirement for a Working Holiday Visa.

How to register your interest If you’re available for an immediate start and would like to be considered as shifts become available, please click APPLY NOW and upload your resume. A consultant will be in touch after reviewing your application.

job.title: Support Needs Assessors
job.description:
Chandler Macleod is seeking experienced Support Needs Assessors to join a Federal Government client on a full-time contract. In this role, you will deliver high-quality, person-centred assessments, working directly with participants to identify and articulate their support needs in a clear, evidence-based and respectful manner.

Key Responsibilities
  • Conduct support needs assessments with participants and their representatives
  • Analyse information and external evidence to support sound, evidence-based decisions
  • Prepare clear, accurate assessment reports
  • Communicate assessment processes and outcomes clearly (virtual and face-to-face)
  • Apply relevant policies, procedures and legislative frameworks
  • Identify and escalate complex or high-risk matters
  • Collaborate with internal stakeholders to support participant outcomes
  • Maintain accurate records using case management systems
  • Adapt assessment approaches to suit individual participant needs
About You You will bring:

  • Strong communication and stakeholder engagement skills
  • Experience in assessment, interviewing or case management
  • Ability to interpret evidence and provide clear, defensible recommendations
  • A commitment to person-centred, inclusive and trauma-informed practice
  • Sound judgement, professionalism and ethical integrity
  • Ability to manage competing priorities and deadlines
  • Experience working within or knowledge of NDIS or similar frameworks (highly regarded)
Essential Requirements
  • Recognised tertiary qualification in a relevant discipline, such as:

    • Occupational Therapy, Physiotherapy, Speech Pathology
    • Social Work, Counselling, Psychology/Psychotherapy
    • Exercise Physiology, Dietetics, Rehabilitation Counselling
    • Nursing (RN/EN), Education-qualified clinicians
    • NDIS Behaviour Support Practitioner
  • Experience in support needs assessments or similar frameworks

  • Understanding of person-centred and strengths-based approaches

job.title: Pump Crew
job.description:
Pump Crew (Dewatering)
Tier 1 Mining Opportunity | 6-Month Fixed Term
Chandler Macleod is seeking experienced Pump Crew / Dewatering Operators to join a tier-one mining operation in Central Queensland.
These are 6-month fixed-term contracts supporting an upcoming wet-season uplift, working Day Shift / Night Shift across operational crews.
What’s on offer
  • $84.64/hr starting rate
  • 6-month fixed-term contract
  • Days & Nights (rotating shifts)
  • Multiple positions available (up to 4 openings)
  • Opportunity to work in a well-established Mine Services environment with strong safety systems and support
Key responsibilities
  • Operate and maintain dewatering / pumping equipment and associated infrastructure
  • Monitor water levels, flows, and pump performance; respond to changing site conditions
  • Conduct routine inspections, basic troubleshooting and minor maintenance
